text:
Dem or Repub, it matters little now.

The US wants the world holding dollars and buying its debt. Preserving the dollar’s reserve currency status is a core strategic interest, and stablecoins give it a way to get dollars into far more hands.

Crypto started with the idea of money outside the state. But as it built this parallel financial system, it turned out that a lot of people simply wanted access to dollars. Someone can use these rails to escape their own government’s monetary control and end up holding American money. Their government doesn’t have to support dollarization for that to happen.

Washington understood the opportunity under Biden. Clearer rules have since given institutions more room to pursue it.

Crypto is stablecoins. Most of the rest is a financial system being built around those dollars, from trading and lending to payments and tokenization. If you want to understand where the opportunities and headwinds lie, you have to understand that dollarization is the core and most of the buildout is downstream of it.

Washington gets a wider market for its currency and debt while retaining leverage through the issuers, reserves and banking relationships connected to its financial system.

Banks and asset managers have customers to win and fees to earn. Their competition helps expand a market the US already has a strategic interest in growing. Those incentives ensure continuity regardless of admin changes

Crypto’s growth now serves interests much older and more powerful than crypto itself. It’s become a pillar of America’s strategy to preserve dollar dominance.

You should probably have exposure here...

quoted_text:
Last night was special.

Election days just never get old for us at Polymarket. Watching regular people experience the beauty of market based forecasts as the results come in. How practically useful it is. How simple it is to interpret. When it clicks, it clicks.

It’s now routinely hours between when prediction markets call it versus the TV networks. The networks hold out until absolute certainty, and the suspense keeps it entertaining all night. No knock to them, but now there’s Polymarket, and many people are realizing they want to know what's happening in real time.

I know the industry has gained a mixed rap for a variety of reasons, many of which are criticisms with real merit. But I think I speak for both myself and my peers when I say we got into this because we really love the idea of markets being able to place a price on the future (e.g. Democrats had a 92% chance to take the House on Polymarket), and how that can help people better understand what's likely to happen and make decisions accordingly.

Our mission is to make sure we deliver on the promise of prediction markets, which was on full display last night. In the midst of so much noise around what we do, the American people get to see what Polymarket is really all about. Feels like one step closer to the dream. Onwards.

text:
NVIDIA Open-Sourced Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents!

Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data.

AI agents can already query databases and retrieve documents.

The harder problem is making sure they understand what the data actually means.

A metric like “revenue” might be defined differently across two systems. The same customer can appear under different identifiers. A generated SQL query can be syntactically correct and still use the wrong business definition.

Auto Ontology is built for that layer in between.

It can build a semantic catalog over enterprise metadata so agents can reason about entities, metrics, relationships, lineage, and where trusted definitions come from.

The workflow is roughly:

Enterprise data + metadata
→ Auto Ontology
→ Semantic catalog / knowledge graph
→ AI agent
→ Grounded query + provenance

It can generate ontologies from existing metadata, connect to semantic models you already have, reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems, and expose that shared context through MCP, CLI, or API.

For structured data, it can also translate natural-language questions into SQL while validating the query against the ontology and certified definitions before returning the result.

So instead of an agent simply asking:

“How much revenue did we generate last month?”

it can understand which revenue definition to use, which tables contain the right data, how those entities relate, and where the final answer came from.

Auto Ontology currently supports relational sources including Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake, and DuckDB.

It also exposes an MCP server, which means agents can query the same semantic layer directly.

For enterprise agents, retrieval alone is not enough.

They also need a shared understanding of what the underlying data actually means.

100% open source.

I’ve shared the GitHub repo in the comments!

quoted_text:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.

text:
Managing Director at UBS, Timothy Arcuri, on why the memory industry has fundamentally changed:

1. Unlike traditional memory which could last for years, HBM is now on an annual development cadence. Each new generation of AI processors requires a specific version of HBM, creating constant, direct connectivity between compute and memory producers. 

2. While logic is used for learning, valuable inference tokens are generated from memory banks, making memory inherently more valuable in an AI context.

3. Major hyperscalers are signing long-term agreements, often including multi-billion dollar prepayments, to secure supply. 

4. The production of HBM is physically more resource-intensive, as it consumes roughly four times the wafer capacity of non-HBM memory due to vertical device stacking. This effectively creates a supply-side anchor, where increased demand for AI compute further constrains available memory supply.

Via @thecompute100

China’s lab-automation roster is a few scaled equipment houses and a long tail of modular liquid-handling / chemistry / manufacturing specialists. 1.MegaRobo — ~9 rounds (peak C ~$1.2B; HK IPO later lapsed); 2024 revenue ~RMB 1B, ~2/3 industrial/semiconductor gear, under RMB 300M “smart lab,” still deep in the red. Products: industrial QC + life-science workcells (platform/integration stack, no single flagship pipettor).

2.Bioyond — Sequoia seed through multi-hundred-million A rounds (Lilly Asia) + 2026 strategic top-up; revenue undisclosed, self-reports 1,000+ customers, Australia via DKSH. Products: LabGenius G3/G5/G7 pipetting, S-series transfer, M-series mobile, LabMate, LabMind — for siRNA, ADC, synbio, proteomics, NGS prep.

3.XR / Xuanren — Angel through reported B (Wuxi state funds); revenue, installs, named customers undisclosed. Product: XR Fluent A25 — 8 independent channels, unequal-volume liquid handling for chemistry/energy labs (earlier mobile-arm + maglev line dropped).

4.XImaging — Through B of over RMB 100M (ByteDance earlier); revenue undisclosed; named showcase Insilico Suzhou Life Star. Products: iMagicOS orchestration (claims 1,000+ brands), HelenX collab arms, colony-picker stations — vision-first integrator.

5.Qingfeng Biochem — Angel then Pre-A of tens of millions (Guangzhou local funds); revenue undisclosed; one self-reported ~RMB 2M win vs imports. Products: OutStanding large pipetting platform, dual liquid-level / non-equal-spacing 8-channel module, BioFlow AI / Supervisor AI, UBLab unattended center.

6.QuikTech — Angel then Pre-A-class rounds (amounts conflict); 2024 “turnover” figures disagree in the tens of millions; first AI-chemistry robot in Singapore. Products: NexoLab (synthesis, sample-prep/analysis, mobile-phase prep), QuikOS scheduling, MoleMind chemistry AI — chemistry/materials, not bio pipettors.

7.Leao Dingfeng — Several rounds through mid-2026 (cumulative “hundreds of millions”); revenue undisclosed; named partners include big Chinese CROs/gene houses. Products: Amphi mid/low-throughput pipetting, high-throughput nanoliter (~50 nL / ~100 nL droplet), flexible stations, RAY Mercury software, DNA/NGS consumables.

8.Innovir — One confirmed ~RMB-hundred-million Series A (WuXi Biologics fund); revenue undisclosed; nearly silent since. Products: closed cell/biologics manufacturing — ImmunoBase full-flow system, INNOFLUID paddle-free reactors, IMMUNOVESSEL consumables (cell, antibody, vaccine, gene therapy). (@sinoinnovel)

9.Zubo Intelligence — No public financing found; likely small Shanghai instruments subsidiary; revenue/customers undisclosed. Products (from patents): micro powder dosing/transfer tools and in-situ synthesis + post-processing workstations.

10.Zhida / InLab — Shenzhen Gaoxintou strategic backing (size undisclosed); revenue undisclosed. Products: online LC-MS sample prep/injection (SPE, headspace, SPME, purge-and-trap, TD, GPC, nitrogen blowdown, etc.) + software to Agilent/Thermo/Shimadzu/SCIEX/Waters/LIMS; also OP275 Pro II olfactometer, Handy TD.

Putting a dollar onchain is useful. Putting an asset onchain is useful. But the real opportunity starts when they can interact.

On Aptos, that's already happening.

Tokenized funds from institutions like @apolloglobal and @BHDigitalAssets bring traditional financial assets onchain.

Credit protocols add lending.

Trading infrastructure creates markets.

Payment platforms connect that ecosystem to users around the world.

That's the bigger idea behind onchain finance. Not simply putting the existing financial system on a blockchain, but making all of its pieces work together.

text:
For those who say it’s time for universal care.  I am all for it. It would be nice if we could find a way to reduce the cost of care and make it available to everyone, for anything. 

But it will take work to get there.  Other countries with Universal Care make “Most Things available to All People”. It’s not perfect. 

In our country, we make “Everything available to Most People”.  

The question for this country, unlike others, is how we can make the best possible care and therapies, regardless of cost, to everyone ? 

Read @AbdulElSayed ‘s book on Medicare for All.  He wisely had more questions than answers.  Medicare for All ? Global Budgets ? Or something else ?

It’s a difficult path from where we are to “E4E” Healthcare. ?Everything for Everyone)

My hope is that we can put together a Simpson Bowles type, Blue Ribbon Commission.  One that includes representatives of all stakeholders.   From all different type of patients.  Including rare disease parents.  Rural and Urban Hospitals.  The most expensive hospitals that offer unique care.  Pharma companies that offer everything from genetics to Cell and Gene Therapies.  You get the point 

Some people think we can just tell all those working in the healthcare system what to do.  

That’s the fastest way for this to fail.  We need to be as close as we can to being on the same page.  And we need to figure out a non partisan manner of running our American version of Universal Care. 

No reason we can’t start now

text:
大模型厂商最怕的，就是你把攒了半年的记忆直接打包带走。

一旦记忆跟模型拆开，所有大模型都会瞬间退化成随时能换的纯算力。

平时用 AI 干活，最折腾人的其实就是上下文割裂。
你在 ChatGPT 里聊透的业务架构，切到 Claude 写文档得重新喂一遍。
在 Cursor 里刚踩过的坑，换到 Claude Code 或 Codex 又得从头交代。
我们被绑在某一家工具上，往往就因为舍不得里面攒下来的那堆历史记录。

今天看到一个叫 Living Brain 的项目，这个团队干了一件特别符合软件工程第一性原理的事：
像当年云计算把存储和计算拆开一样，在模型和 Agent 框架外面，单独架了一层可读写的外置大脑。

通过 MCP 或 API 接进去之后，你在 ChatGPT 里存下的结论，打开 Claude 就能直接调出来，切到自己的 Agent 框架里还能接着用。
谁家模型今天降价、谁家写代码更顺手，随时切过去就行，反正脑子跟着你走。

之前很多做长期记忆的工具用起来挺鸡肋，主要卡在两个死穴上：
要么不管三七二十一全塞进上下文，贵得要死还抓不住重点。
要么记忆存久了会“发臭”，三个星期前早就改掉的旧方案，Agent 还在那当圣旨用。

我看了一下这玩意的设计，确实有点东西。

它借鉴了神经可塑性的机制，每条信息进来先过四道打分：
值不值得存、该放哪、跟已有知识怎么连、对当前任务有没有用。
按他们内部在 LongMemEval-S 和 LoCoMo 上的评测数据：
原本要塞 116K 全量上下文的任务，它平均只调取 5.1K。
单次提问消耗的 Token 少了 22.6 倍，单任务成本直接砍掉 95%，检索中位数延迟 464 毫秒，准确率能干到 92.2%。

更戳中工程痛点的是，它给记忆加了新鲜度、维护压力和可用度三个体检指标。
哪些知识过期了、哪些地方攒出了冲突，在 Agent 拿去闯祸之前，你能先一眼看出来。

当然这事也有边界。
上面那套漂亮数据毕竟是官方内部评测跑出来的，而且它自己的 API 输入定价是 8 美元每百万 Token，单看单价真不算便宜。
如果你平时只是随手问几个单次问题，搞这套外置大脑纯属杀鸡用牛刀。
只有当你重度依赖多工具协同，每天在好几个 Agent 和不同模型之间来回横跳、每次重建上下文都想砸键盘的时候，省下来的那二十多倍 Token 和折腾时间才真的划算。

但我觉得这个方向给所有做 AI 产品的提了个醒：
当模型本身的智商差距越抹越平，未来真正值钱的壁垒，是谁能管好用户那套不断生长、又不会腐烂的活体记忆。

这么看下来，以后这颗赛博外置大脑大概率比我本人的脑子条理清楚多了，要不我以后干脆腾出脑容量去记哪家菜市场打折，每天只负责给它充五块钱电费算了。

author: laopai1990
quoted_text:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://t.co/KowVVCSPp8

text:
Security and fraud concerns are often aligned but sometimes they run counter. The 2017-2022 crypto onramp craze is a great example, and I think we’ll see the same phenomenon with Agentic commerce:

Yesterday I asked which of these 4 payment methods had the highest fraud rates to purchase crypto in the US

1. ACH
2. Debit cards
3. Apple/Google Pay
4. Wires

Most people guessed ACH or debit cards. But the answer is number 3, Apple & Google Pay wallets.

Wallets had the worst fraud despite the best security, for 2 reasons:

1. Wallet tokenization design was built with mostly security in mind and ignored fraud concerns

When you add a card to a wallet, its 16-digit card number (PAN) is replaced with a device-specific number (D-PAN). The D-PAN doesn’t keep the card’s first 6–8 digits, the BIN, which merchants use to identify the issuing bank.

Each bank’s tokens did get their own new BIN range, so the issuer was still technically identifiable. But merchants had no way to map those new ranges back to a bank name.

That broke a common fraud control. Merchants keep blocklists of issuers with weak fraud controls and decline their cards. Without knowing the issuer, those blocklists stopped working for wallet transactions.

2. Wallet tokenization made some fraud velocity checks meaningless

The other fundamental issue with D-PAN was that it was device bound. A fraudster could take the same card, add it to 1000s of devices and generate all new D-PANs.

Basically, they used the same card over and over but it looked different each time.

***

What did we build to counteract these issues?

(I promise we'll get to agentic commerce!)

It took us several years to get to the bottom of this and countless conversations with Apple, Google, Visa and Mastercard.

The solution that we & the industry now use:

1. New tokenization method called M-PAN which is a merchant bound token to prevent a fraudster from creating 1000s of D-PANs from the same card number.

2. Visa created a new API called Payment Account Reference, which lets you identify if two D-PANs are connected to the same PAN.

3. New mapping built from D-PAN BIN ranges to identify issuers, so “issuer name” based rules still work.

These solutions are available to our merchants who use us for fraud prevention on wallet transactions.

***

The question we’re now asking: what does this mean for Agentic commerce?

History is repeating itself. Agentic shopping is essentially introducing a new actor, an Agent, to whom you need to hand over your card. In many ways, an Agent appears like a wallet.

We’re very likely to see similar fraud vectors like adding a stolen card to 100s of Agents and generating a new D-PAN for each of them to shop.

As Agent builders figure out how to tokenize the consumer’s card, our suggestion would be to use M-PAN over D-PAN.

If you need help with all this, reach out. We’re building solutions to these problems at @sardine — more to come this week! — and are here to help and brainstorm.

一觉醒来又刷到一家科技中厂的裁员噩耗。设计平台 Canva 今天宣布了成立 13 年以来的第一次裁员：全球共 1271 名员工被裁，占员工总数的 22%。

翻了一圈今天领英上 Laid off 的帖子，粗略估算被裁的 50% 以上都是传统 UI/UX Designer。随着各种 AI 工具的成熟，平台原先的付费用户逐渐抛弃传统绘图方式，转而使用各种 AI 生成的图片。Canva 增长预期腰斩，设计需求断崖式下跌，自然无力供养设计师们。

想起我第一次使用 Canva 的经历：在加拿大读书的时候，每周至少要做两份小组展示，组员们默认都使用 Canva，因为联网同步修改 PPT 很方便，设计组件也很灵活，比之前在国内的用的 PowerPoint 好用且好看。

和同等体量的科技中厂比起来，Canva 一直走“小而美”路线。但没想到 AI 的冲击下，看起来再“精致”的公司，也只能断臂求生。

quoted_text:
Releasing Delta League: edit LLM weights for benchmarking and glory! Join at deltaleague(.)ai

Earlier this week, the idea of editing weights directly with an LLM got a lot of attention —
but it was shunted by limitations in the demonstrated approach.

Delta League is an open competition for everyone to submit deltas to model weights and get them scored on a hidden test set. Auto-research and hillclimb to make smaller models more performant.

The broader vision for Delta League is creating a platform for open AI research. Beyond just editing weights, this approach offers verifiable evaluation and an open collaborative space for everyone to continue improving Pareto of open source models.

In the coming days, we will extend this platform to support editing model architectures beyond just weights and custom evaluation sets to understand how models perform in specific domains and for businesses.

text:
说真的，我想杀了我的 bot

AI 发展到今天真是让人又爱又恨。爱，处理各种确定性的、重复性的、单一的任务太好用了，完美取代了很多人工；恨，一旦涉及到有争议的、有取向的、有复杂关系或策略的完全就乱套了，给我一通瞎搞。

最典型的就是交易，完全跟着 AI 策略走？亏不死你。

让我们潜入！

⬇️

冯小刚在《非诚勿扰》借用了彭浩翔指导的电影《青春梦工厂》里一个经典桥段，葛优饰演的海归秦奋发明了一个人类分歧终端机，最终获得了200万英镑投资。这个发明妙啊，双方把手伸进一个桶里，石头剪刀布然后打开桶，这样就没法作弊了，绝了。

事实上，分歧的解决并没有这么简单，尤其是在 AI 时代。很多人不知道，比特币的发明其实源于解决双花困境的分歧，数学 + 区块链 + AI，人类在解决分歧、争议的路上正在大踏步前进。那到底要解决什么的分歧、又如何解决呢？

就我个人而言，我用了大量的交易 bot 在辅助我交易，那个蠢啊！其实它非常善于执行既定策略，但智能合约只能回答 YES/NO，预言机大部分只擅长传递数据，当 AI 遇到交易需要「合理」调仓、分配杠杠的时候、当预测市场出现模糊争议结论的时候、当出现多个信息源标准不一的时候……

争议产生了，如何解决？还记得 「 Optimism Democracy 乐观民主 」吗？简单总结流程就是随机选出不同背景的验证者达成共识，然后对争议进行挑战、申诉、升级处理直到解决。如果放到 AI 背景下，就是：

不同模型的 AI 验证者 → 多人复合  →  链上上诉   →  争议解决。再展开一点，跟法庭有点类似，协议会随机选取一个模型的验证者当领导，这样可以避免被单一模型操控（现在很泛滥了）。

.@OpenAI 不满足于让 AI 写代码了，现在连 @github 的生意也想抢。

OpenAI 宣布收购开发工具初创公司 Pierre Computer，准备将其代码托管能力整合进 Codex。

这笔收购的关键不只是两款开源工具 Trees 和 Diffs，而是 Pierre 的商业产品 Code Storage：支持代码仓库创建、版本历史管理和 API 接入，让多个 AI Agent 可以同时操作代码。

Lovable、Bolt、Amp 等 AI 编程产品已经在使用这套服务。

与此同时，OpenAI 自研的代码管理系统 Pando 也已投入内部使用，代码推送中位耗时缩短近 80%。

收购完成后，Pierre 现有开源项目将继续开源，Code Storage 则逐步接入 Codex。

这意味着 OpenAI 的竞争边界正在扩大：从 AI 帮你写代码，到 AI 帮你管理代码、协作开发，甚至托管整个代码仓库。

GitHub 面对的，可能不再只是 AI 编程工具的竞争，而是整个开发者工作流的重构。

author: alexocheema
quoted_text:
AI is using more and more of the world’s energy. But how much economic value are we getting from AI?

We’re introducing Joules-to-GDP (J2G), a framework that measures how well AI turns energy into economic value and shows which tasks, models, and hardware give the best return.

Across 44 occupations in finance, engineering, law, administrative work, and more in @OpenAI's GDPval, we arrive at three findings:

1) The tasks with the highest economic value are not the tasks with the highest economic value per joule. For example, CAD design earns ~10% more per task than building websites, but the latter earns ~27% more value per joule.

2) The most powerful model isn’t always the best use of energy. Gemma 4 31B delivers 56% of GLM 5.2’s net value with 23% of the energy, for 2.5x the value per joule.

3) More chips don’t guarantee proportionate returns. Moving the same model from 1 to 8 NVIDIA H100s uses 3.2x the energy but cuts completion time by only 22%, with about the same value.

With @SnorkelAI, we’re also releasing GDPWorks, a benchmark for economically valuable tasks across 36 additional occupations.

Joint work co-led by @amirzeinaalii and @Avanika15, with @Mersad_Abbasi, @Jon_Hartley_, John Hennessy, @HazyResearch, and @Azaliamirh.

More details below 🧵

As a gentleman and a scholar of the cold war, here are my 2 kopeyeks

> 4) Change our relationship to Israel

This is unfortunately cooked.  Since ww2 Russian/soviet strategy has been to control energy exports to Western Europe.  Almost immediate post ww2 they backed Assads, Ba’ath party, Sadat, you name it.  

USA/west and arguably even China just want reliable markets for energy.  That’s all.  When the media says it’s all about the “oil”, this is the part they leave out.  USA doesn’t want to control the oil fields and they don’t care who is their shareholder.  They don’t even care if prices are high because if it’s an open fair market high prices will drive investment and more energy will flow.  

Putin doesn’t want this because open fair market runs around any geopolitical leverage. He wants to control the oil fields so he can influence Europe.  There is zero ideological overlap between Putin and irgc, yet they are allies, and for this reason. 

There isn’t going to be some deep China/russia alliance for this reason, because last thing China wants is 5k nuke armed russia with any leverage over its high employment manufacturing industry.  

So wtf is Israel involved in any of this? It’s really hard to build an army that’s effective at blowing up Russian tanks and SAMs.  USSR sent a ton of arms into Syria and Egypt in the 50s and Kennedy had basically terrible options to counter Soviet arms build up.  The alternatives were so bad that a Boston Irish catholic in the 50s armed Israel.  

Why aren’t there any good alternatives? A competent general and officer core is a challenge to any regime. ME armies are built around supporting internal security and providing stability for the regime, and not executing multi pronged complex missions.  Good general + good officers + shitty civil government = coup

Israel is not likely to undergo a military coup, so the civil administration has no fear of a competent defense force.  So their army is good at blowing up Russian tanks and SAMs. Turkey is probably the closest alternative.  

Nothing has changed since the Cold War.  Putin wants leverage over Europe and China if he can get it, irgc want leverage over SA and gcc and Israel is the main USA armed neighborhood police.  

What are the options? 

1) usa disconnects from ME and EU. We have a ton of oil in americas so high prices or not the spice will flow and we don’t care about Putins leverage, let them all deal with it on their own. 

2) SA/gcc/turkey/jordan all heavily invest into high functioning armies. Turkey is the closest and imho, a war between turkey and irgc would be at least as bad as the Ukraine war today. As much as everyone in ME dislikes Israel my guess is that there isn’t a ton of love for the former ottomans.  

3) China takes over somehow. This is totally far fetched and would scare the crap out of even the most nativist dem or gop. 

4) France/europe? It’s so cooked I think 3 is more likely.  You can’t afford 50%+ gdp welfare state and a navy
author: toly
quoted_text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

We hope it is a meaningful step toward democratizing general-purpose robots capable of operating in complex, real-world environments.

The recently disclosed FomoPeek security incident and DarkSword exploit toolkit are important reminders to keep iOS devices secure:

◾️ FomoPeek: According to SlowMist, versions 1.1–1.2 were found to contain malicious code that could exploit iOS vulnerabilities, escape the system sandbox, and access data from other apps.

◾️ DarkSword: A recently disclosed iOS exploit toolkit that could use malicious links or compromised websites to exploit unpatched vulnerabilities, gain access to a device, and extract sensitive data.

Although their attack vectors differ, both pose risks at the device and operating system level. Even if a wallet itself has no vulnerabilities, sensitive data may still be at risk on an infected or outdated device.

🛡️ To help protect your assets, we strongly recommend:

🔹 Update iOS to the latest version for your device 
🔹 Remove FomoPeek and any other suspicious apps 
🔹 Avoid unfamiliar links and untrusted websites 
🔹 Download apps only from official sources

If you installed or used FomoPeek 1.1–1.2, create a new wallet on a clean, fully updated device and transfer your assets ASAP. For additional protection against device-level risks, consider using a @KeyPalWallet hardware wallet for larger holdings.
author: pan_tokenpocket
quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

author: gajria
quoted_text:
Compute will become worthless.

The GPU barons spending billions on compute farms today are akin to the carriage barons of the 1900s that spent building out infrastructure for horse carriages, lengthening the bottleneck, blind to the machine that’s coming to widen it.

Trade: the DuPont family started buying General Motors stock in 1914, when the auto industry was still young and one that was treated as a niche.

I.e., compute becoming valuable because AI feeds on it is not a moat, but a bounty, an incentive for engineers to solve its scarcity.

1. AI demand makes compute scarce.
2. Scarcity makes compute extremely profitable.
3. Profit attracts capital into photonics, neuromorphic chips, wafer-scale chips, better memory, better cooling, better networking, better algorithms.
4. Compute gets cheaper per unit.

As better ways to compute, better means to produce compute, or better ways to use compute arise, all the capex we burnt on traditional compute will go to waste, leaving dead assets in the books of several corporations.

In the 1800s, agriculture depended heavily on natural nitrogen sources like Peruvian guano and Chilean nitrates. These were scarce, and inconveniently located making them geopolitically strategic. Then, two german chemists, Haber and Bosch, developed a way to fix nitrogen from the air into ammonia, with lab success in 1909 and industrial scale by 1913. The previous scarcity, “where do we find enough nitrogen?” (Akin to “where do we find enough GPUs”), was attacked by an advancement: Industrial chemistry.

History was made last night.

For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes. 

Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with.

2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here?

When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn’t turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We’ve lost the House. We’ve lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats.

We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there’s Texas.

Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven’t had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we’ll have both.

Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today.

Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, “It’s not about you. It’s about them. It’s about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures.” Too many politicians forget that.

Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here’s what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas.

Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters. 
Corruption. Number two, 18.5%. 
The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%. 
The candidates are terrible, 7.9%. 
The Canada trade war, 7.6%. 
The GOP didn’t do enough to support Trump, 6.6%. 
Republicans didn’t pass the Save America Act, 5.6%. 
Trump’s focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%.

The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn’t understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don’t tell all of the story.

Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel’s processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That’s double the share just two years ago.

In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm.

And here’s one that’s really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That’s another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries.

That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn’t understand or they didn’t care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.

Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars.

There’s a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world’s very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American’s electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years.

Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn’t do enough to address their very real pain.

So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people’s lives, and we need to deal with the consequences.

Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That’s not something I ever thought I would say.

We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk.

And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed.

Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI.

The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They’ll just blame it all on Donald Trump.

In the next two years, we need to do two things.

One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they’re willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.

So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution.

And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost.

There’s a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn’t show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics.

For Hispanics, there’s a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around.

And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record.

Too few voters were even aware of what we’d accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism.

People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else.

But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain’t us. Texas is still Texas.

We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well.

When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America.

It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you.

text:
What makes Percolator Trade different from Phoenix, Hyper Liquid and other perp DEXs?

On most perp DEXs, every market shares one pool of risk: one margin system, one insurance fund, one pool of liquidity.

A blowup in one thin market can drain capital that backs every other market. So those venues have to be conservative. They list a small set of large assets, they decide centrally what gets listed, and new tokens wait  or never get listed at all.

With Percolator Trade,

Markets sit in isolated pools, each with its own liquidity and risk buffer. If one market goes bad, the loss stays there and can’t spread to the rest of the protocol. That isolation is what lets us do what the others structurally can’t:

Permissionless listing: Anyone can launch a market on any token in a few clicks, without waiting for governance or a listing team.

Long-tail first: A token can have a leveraged market long before the big venues would consider it, because listing it doesn't put anyone else's capital at risk.

LPs choose their risk: Liquidity providers back the specific markets they want and earn those markets' fees, rather than being exposed to everything.

Underneath that is the Percolator risk engine, the open source engine published by Toly.  It is designed to keep each market solvent on its own, even where liquidity is thin. 

Phoenix and the others are good at being the venue for majors. 

We're building the venue for everything else.
author: PercolatorTrade

I believe we'll see a slow shift, with whales buying only Float coins.

The downside: far fewer coins will bond.

But the ones that do will likely be much higher quality than pump coins, and that's where the whales will focus.

Expect to see all ‘good’ attention coins to run the highest on float.

- 项目评价：产品已经很成熟了，不用担心小团队跑路。以后生态发射台一堆，用它交易最省心。

5⃣DeriveXYZ（ @DeriveXYZ ）
- 项目定位：专门做链上期权的平台，交易 BTC、ETH、HYPE 等。
- 项目评分：8.6/10
- 参与机会：主网第一天就开，还有跟 Kinetiq 一起的交易赛（奖 kHYPE）。
- 项目评价：期权赛道头部玩家，官方也强推。Elysium 速度快，特别适合这种专业交易产品。

6⃣HybraFinance + Navo（ @HybraFinance /  @navodotfamily ）
- 项目定位：Hybra 是 Hyperliquid 上已经有的流动性平台，Navo 是他们做的社区发射台。
- 项目评分：8.5/10
- 参与机会：主网第一天就部署，Navo 发币创建者能拿 70% 交易费。
- 项目评价：老项目了，社区所有权做得比较实在。发射台和流动性绑定在一起，不是纯炒作，后面有持续玩法。

7⃣Stockium（ @Stockium ）
- 项目定位：发币时可以直接跟股票代币配对，还能让持币人分到股票。
- 项目评分：8.3/10
- 参与机会：测试网已经在活跃，有回购销毁记录，还能用他们的交易终端。
- 项目评价：玩法比较新，持币直接分股票这个点有意思。团队也比较活跃，回购销毁能查到链上记录。

8⃣eleosfun（ @eleosfun ）
- 项目定位：功能比较全的发射台，支持多种发币方式，也能跟股票配对。
- 项目评分：8.2/10
- 参与机会：测试网期间发币几乎不花钱（他们帮你出 Gas），持币能自动分 HYPE。
- 项目评价：玩法设计得比较细，反狙击和持有者友好机制都做了，比很多纯土狗发射台用心。

9⃣BunnyPad（ @Bunnypadfun ）
- 项目定位：主打「公平发射」的发射台，一笔交易发完，没有团队预留，池子永久锁定。
- 项目评分：8.0/10
- 参与机会：测试网交易和发射都能拿积分，主网可能有空投资格。
- 项目评价：测试网交易量不小，公平机制是它的最大卖点，我挺看好这个平台发射出来的项目

🔟Oxley（ @oxleydotfun ）
- 项目定位：用拍卖的方式来发币，让价格更公平一点。
- 项目评分：7.9/10
- 参与机会：测试网可以参与拍卖，找 Bug 还能拿 HYPE 奖励。
- 项目评价：增长数据不错，是真有人在用。解决了传统发射容易被控盘的问题，产品迭代也比较快。

1⃣1⃣aka. fun（ @akadotfun ）
- 项目定位：用 Uniswap V4 做的发射台，主打 Meme + 真实资产奖励。
- 项目评分：7.8/10
- 参与机会：测试网已经上线，可以直接玩。
- 项目评价：测试网活跃度还可以，粉丝也不少。后面跟真实资产结合是它的看点。

1⃣2⃣PerpMe（ @perpmefun ）
- 项目定位：用 Uniswap V3 做的发射台，支持跟股票代币配对，还有早期桥接功能。
- 项目评分：7.7/10
- 参与机会：测试网就能发币交易，也可以提前体验桥。
- 项目评价：比较早的玩家，创建者拿的手续费比例高。适合喜欢短线的人看看。

1⃣3⃣Elyziumaa（ @Elyziumaa ）
- 项目定位：现在测试网上比较火的 NFT 系列，挂在 Kalos 上交易。
- 项目评分：7.5/10
- 参与机会：可以去抢白名单和 Mint，之后在 Kalos 上交易。
- 项目评价：NFT 热度在前面，叙事跟生态贴得比较紧，有 Kalos 撑着，流动性相对稳一些。

1⃣4⃣Hyperion_RPG（ @Hyperion_RPG ）
- 项目定位：风险越高奖励越高的链上 RPG 游戏。
- 项目评分：7.3/10
- 参与机会：测试网就能玩，主网上线后有排行榜奖励。
- 项目评价：游戏方向比较少见，玩法有点意思。生态里游戏还不多，有一定差异化。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
昨晚的美股很强势但板块也是在分化：道指大涨约3%创下44年来最强的中期选举后单日表现，标普等权+1.86%强于标普500的1.5%，罗素2000涨幅也高于纳指。道指明显强于纳指，说明涨幅在向传统蓝筹、消费、医疗等板块扩散。而整个科技板块分化则很明显：超大云厂大科技非常强势、部分软件/saas走势很好，但半导体和电力板块整体走弱。说说我的理解：
1、看起来市场认为“中选结束+分裂政府（民主党掌控国会+川普继续当总统）”是个好事：
一方面政策不确定性大大降低；
另一方面分裂政府也会让政策极端化风险降低市场更偏好“有制衡的华盛顿”；
而油价大跌，布油跌倒94原因则是市场认为伊朗战争可能降温（这个迹象值得继续关注）。

昨晚走势非常典型地体现了“政治不确定性消除 + AI交易内部分化”这两件事。

2、民主党掌控国会对企业意味着什么？
1）政策波动减小：过去两年共和党一党独大时，关税、监管、地缘政策变化很快、很猛。现在国会被民主党掌控，很多激进动作会被卡住，市场喜欢这种“少折腾”。
2）行业板块受益点：
（1）医疗、医院类股票大涨（市场预期民主党可能部分逆转之前的医保削减）；
（2）消费、零售（尤其服务低收入人群的）表现好；
（3）油价大跌对能源股是利空，但对航空、运输、消费等传统行业是利好。

3）但民主党在数据中心、AI基建、环境监管上更严格，对能源、部分工业和基建节奏会有压制。
所以市场更多是在交易“不确定性降低”和“油价回落”，但并不是说预期民主党会大幅刺激传统产业。

3、再重点聊聊科技板块内部的AI分化
1）民主党在德州、乔治亚等关键州取得进展，这些地方对数据中心的社区反对声浪很大。市场担心数据中心建设节奏会放缓（环境、电力、水资源、监管审查更严），从而影响半导体硬件需求增速。

而大厂本身算力积累够，又是承载AI商业化的主体，反而可能因为新建放缓而相对受益（减少资本开支压力，强化现有优势）。

2）软件股有些表现不错，则说明资金进一步把关注点从“谁在建数据中心/卖芯片”转向“谁能真正把AI变现、做出商业化产品”。
这是典型的AI交易从“基建周期”向“应用与变现”分化的迹象。

4、关于科技板块分化这一点
这里要把上周在168X的访谈里聊到的AI主线迁移的观点再搬出来（见配图），访谈内容在这里https://t.co/l0MotcPBA2。

核心逻辑还是“AI主线迁移，每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，部署越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。”

但大家很容易形成的定式思维是什么？
一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。完全把AI = Semiconductor = Memory划等号，其实并非如此。AI也分上中下游，越往后中游的大云厂，下游的应用、agent会更受益以及各种应用场景。这也是7月份这里https://t.co/68oy5mSQ1z聊AI进入工程化阶段的必然趋势。

半导体有没有机会？跌多了跌出了性价比，那么机会也就出来了。只是说应该没有新的主线那么强势和丝滑。而且现在市场计价的是民主党上台就让数据中心建设减速，如昨天这里https://t.co/2F8dNnVKh6聊到的得州新当选的民主党州长对数据中心的要求上，也并没那么糟糕、而且要到27年1月初新党员的议员和州长才能正式履新。所以需要关注，什么时候市场开始意识到这一点、对半导体认知发生改观。年底前半导体可能会有一波反弹的机会。

text:
So happy for @the_bunny_chen and the @FireworksAI_HQ team. 

The growth angle here is easy to underestimate: 

1. For AI apps, your most engaged users can also be your most expensive to serve. Cheaper, task-specific models give you room to offer more usage, experiment with pricing, and reach customers who were previously uneconomical.
The interesting loop is turning that usage into better models. 

2. Accepted suggestions, corrections, and repeat attempts can help reveal what users actually value: provided you can distinguish a useful signal from a noisy one.

3. Making that loop accessible to small teams could change how AI apps compound: every customer interaction becomes a chance to improve both the product and its economics
author: laura_llin
quoted_text:
@the_bunny_chen (CO-FOUNDER @ @FireworksAI_HQ) ON TRAINING WITHOUT EVALS, GPUS OR A RESEARCH TEAM

Training is now an economics play for app companies
- For AI apps, sustained usage costs, not acquisition costs, are what limit scale, and a custom model fixes that. 
- Contrast this to Web 2.0, where the main cost was user acquisition (Facebook/Instagram ads) and serving each extra user cost almost nothing.

Cheaper models are a growth enabler, not just a cost saving
- Cheaper models -> more users -> more data and better evals -> faster scaling.
- Founders care most about wall-clock time. They'll choose a slightly more expensive training run if it gets a better result sooner.
- Fireworks reuses training recipes across customers, so startups don't repeat each other's mistakes.

"No Eval": teams can start training without writing offline evals. Your traffic is the training signal
- Writing evals by hand is the biggest blocker to training your own model. Benny said “we don’t have evals” comes up in ~90% of his customer conversations.
- No Eval turns production traces and user signals (thumbs up/down, picking A vs. B, accepted suggestions) into task-specific evals → shows where the model falls short → measures whether training closed the gap.
- Now in private preview.

Serverless RL: train and serve custom models with no GPUs, paid per token
- Until now, doing RL meant managing GPU quotas, choosing hardware and getting configs right, or the run would “go haywire.”
- Fireworks now handles all of that: serverless trainers, plus serverless samplers for the RL loop, billed per token.

Fireworks Lab: Fireworks researchers embedded in your team, paid on outcomes
- For companies that aren’t ready to self-serve. Benny called it a “graduation process” that leads onto the platform.
- Pricing is tied to outcomes, not training spend, so customers don’t worry Fireworks just wants their compute budget.

When not to train? If the tokens aren’t core to your business, don’t bother
- Low-stakes, everyday use doesn’t need a custom model. Use an off-the-shelf option like Nexus, which picks a model for you (note: self-serving 😅)
- Train if model quality drives your unit economics or how happy your customers are. That’s your “alpha,” and you need to build it into the model, through the weights or the harness around it.

2027 prediction: open models close the gap as they get more compute

text:
英国金融科技巨头 Revolut 把 2000 名程序员从 Claude Code 迁到自建中国开源模型 GLM，成本砍掉 90%，开发交付时间反而缩短了 70%
在纽约举办的 AI Engineer 大会上，欧洲估值最高的金融科技独角兽之一 Revolut 公开了一组内部架构迁移数据。公司 AI 运营与基础设施负责人 David Abitbol 透露，他们已经将旗下约 2000 名软件工程师的默认编程工具，从 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和 OpenAI 的 Codex 切换到了自建服务器部署的智谱开源模型 GLM（从 GLM-5.1 升级至 GLM-5.3）。
这一刀切下去，Revolut 只用了 56 张英伟达 B200 显卡，就把内部综合推理成本压到了每百万 Token 约 0.30 美元，直接把付给 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的账单砍掉了 90%。
【为什么放着顶级的 Claude 不用？】
Revolut 最早从 2025 年 2 月开始试用 Claude Code，并在 2026 年 1 月全员铺开，但很快撞上了残酷的经济账。当时部分重度使用的工程师每人每月要烧掉 1000 到 10000 美元的 API 费用，但公司整体研发效率并没有看到对等的产出。
为了止血，公司被迫给每位工程师设了每月 300 美元的严格额度上限。结果这引发了第二个尴尬的后遗症：因为怕额度不够用，程序员们开始像省粮票一样把 Token 攒着留给最难的代码硬骨头，平时顺手能用 AI 提效的杂活反而不敢用了。
Abitbol 在演讲中点出了一个被很多技术团队忽视的真相：“工程研发的瓶颈其实不在于纯写代码的速度。”真正拖慢程序员的，往往是淹没在收件箱、Jira 工单、Confluence 文档和上下文切换里的时间。换成固定成本的自建开源模型后，公司彻底取消了额度限制，工程师开始肆无忌惮地用 AI 处理周边杂活。从 4 月切到自建架构以来，Revolut 测算内部编码时间缩短了约 60%，从接单到合并代码的整体交付周期（Lead Time）缩短了 70%。
【56 张 B200 显卡是怎么调教出来的】
作为一家受严格监管的数字银行，使用中国团队开源的模型难免面临合规审视。Abitbol 对此的解法很直接：“中国开源权重，西方自有服务器”——只下载公开的模型权重，跑在 Revolut 自己位于美国的隔离基础设施上，完全不经过外部托管服务；遇到视觉图片任务则分流给 Gemini，而昂贵的 Claude Code 和 Codex 依然保留，但只作为攻克极少数顶尖难题的“特批武器”。
刚把模型权重塞进显卡时，开箱即用的推理体验非常糟糕，首字延迟（TTFT）高达 14.26 秒。团队没有盲目加显卡，而是花了四个月死磕底层推理优化：
• 将上下文窗口上限锁定在 256K Token，并保证代码场景下 90% 以上的缓存命中率（Cache Hit Rate）。
• 在 Blackwell 架构上采用 NVFP4 量化格式替代 FP8，在几乎不损失精度的前提下节省了约 40% 的显存占用。
调优完成后，在不增加一张显卡的情况下，系统每秒处理的请求量提升了 76%，首字响应时间从 14.26 秒直接压到了 1.68 秒。按市面租金估算，56 张 B200 显卡每月的租赁成本大约在 24.5 万到 32.7 万美元之间，平摊到 2000 名工程师头上，每人每月只需 120 到 165 美元左右，就能实现全员不限量的高速代码辅助。

text:
很多人以为临近 IPO 熬到套现是稳赚的买卖，但核心骨干选在最风光的时候接连撤退，逻辑其实很残酷。Cat Wu 和 Thariq 相继离开，绝不是单纯的职业换道，而是产品的红利期和研发团队的创作期彻底错位了。

从 0 到 1 验证 Agent 架构的造神阶段已经收尾，现在各家拼的全是填坑脏活：压 token 成本、调状态同步、给动不动就崩的 harness 擦屁股。工具越来越自动化，背后工程师的自由度反而被各种监控和交付 KPI 锁死，谁干谁身心俱疲。

骨干团队在这个节点交接，往往意味着技术探索期结束、商业变现期开打，接下来的产品大概率少有颠覆性惊喜，更多是额度收紧与功能切块卖钱的琐碎日常。

author: twid
quoted_text:
AI is using more and more of the world’s energy. But how much economic value are we getting from AI?

We’re introducing Joules-to-GDP (J2G), a framework that measures how well AI turns energy into economic value and shows which tasks, models, and hardware give the best return.

Across 44 occupations in finance, engineering, law, administrative work, and more in @OpenAI's GDPval, we arrive at three findings:

1) The tasks with the highest economic value are not the tasks with the highest economic value per joule. For example, CAD design earns ~10% more per task than building websites, but the latter earns ~27% more value per joule.

2) The most powerful model isn’t always the best use of energy. Gemma 4 31B delivers 56% of GLM 5.2’s net value with 23% of the energy, for 2.5x the value per joule.

3) More chips don’t guarantee proportionate returns. Moving the same model from 1 to 8 NVIDIA H100s uses 3.2x the energy but cuts completion time by only 22%, with about the same value.

With @SnorkelAI, we’re also releasing GDPWorks, a benchmark for economically valuable tasks across 36 additional occupations.

Joint work co-led by @amirzeinaalii and @Avanika15, with @Mersad_Abbasi, @Jon_Hartley_, John Hennessy, @HazyResearch, and @Azaliamirh.

author: PercolatorTrade
quoted_text:
What makes Percolator Trade different from Phoenix, Hyper Liquid and other perp DEXs?

On most perp DEXs, every market shares one pool of risk: one margin system, one insurance fund, one pool of liquidity.

A blowup in one thin market can drain capital that backs every other market. So those venues have to be conservative. They list a small set of large assets, they decide centrally what gets listed, and new tokens wait  or never get listed at all.

With Percolator Trade,

Markets sit in isolated pools, each with its own liquidity and risk buffer. If one market goes bad, the loss stays there and can’t spread to the rest of the protocol. That isolation is what lets us do what the others structurally can’t:

Permissionless listing: Anyone can launch a market on any token in a few clicks, without waiting for governance or a listing team.

Long-tail first: A token can have a leveraged market long before the big venues would consider it, because listing it doesn't put anyone else's capital at risk.

LPs choose their risk: Liquidity providers back the specific markets they want and earn those markets' fees, rather than being exposed to everything.

Underneath that is the Percolator risk engine, the open source engine published by Toly.  It is designed to keep each market solvent on its own, even where liquidity is thin. 

Phoenix and the others are good at being the venue for majors. 

We're building the venue for everything else.

text:
The current pace of development in mathematics is incredible. Independent researchers and AI labs are formalizing large swaths of mathematical infrastructure. But there is one catch: understanding Lean does not always feel natural.

After a period of preparation, I am excited to launch a new project, 

Agentic Approach to Computer Algebra Systems, 

generously supported by Renaissance Philanthropy through its AI for Math Fund 2026.

The project will be shared between Adam Mickiewicz University and Warsaw University of Technology. Over the next two years, we will focus on building tools and experiences for mathematicians who want to work smoothly with AI agents and formalized mathematics without losing the flexibility of pen-and-paper exploration that they enjoyed so much in the past.

For me personally, this is the start of a new adventure, where the challenge is very much like that of a start-up. We will build our solution in the ever-changing landscape of increasingly powerful AI agents. I believe there is still value in work done by mathematicians for other mathematicians.

Let me know if you are interested in getting in touch, whether to collaborate or simply share some kind words, ideas, or opportunities to join forces on more cross-disciplinary projects.

$CRCL 财报那么亮眼，为什么还静悄悄裁员？

$CRCL 第三季度财报出了，营收 8.65 亿美元，同比 +17 % 
每股收益 0.84 美元，是市场预期的两倍，
净利润是 2.26 亿美元，调整后 EBITDA 涨 85 %。

为啥还裁员 5 % 呢？
财报的原话是为了更好地匹配运营模式和战略重点。

我们一步步继续剖析，
这 8.65 亿里，有 1.82 亿是 Arc 链的 ARC 代币预售，
这是一次性的卖币收入。
如果撇除卖币， 同比营收是 - 7.7 %，真正的净利润大约只剩 4400 万美元。
而我们之前一直嫌弃的吃老本，这轮也不好吃了，
因为储备收益率从 4.11 % 掉到了 3.5 % ，这轮储备利息收入跌了 8 %

上半年每赚 1 美元，就得拿 0.59 美元分给币安、Coinbase 等分销伙伴， 
这个季度是 0.60 美元，一分没省，还倒涨了。
光这季度就分出去 4.12 亿美元。

核心收入在减少，开始削减开支。
现在整个加密行业都在裁员，是趁报表好看的时候修成本也是无可厚非。
老问题还是在一样， 第三季度 96 % 还是靠着储备资产利息，
这轮就开始应验我们之前讲的，储备收益率一跌，收入就开始减少了。

我是一位不喜欢打嘴炮的分析师，我相信自己的判断。我的每一篇数据分析，都只服务于我个人的交易需求。

目前看，运气好，零失误。

好了，现在我买了，以后你们别再问我ETH了，因为很可能我说的只是内心意愿的表达，而不是客观数据的反馈。

text:
越聪明的模型越会选择理性妥协，而非原则性坚持

在资源分配任务里，前沿模型独自掌握双方需求时，100% 能找到团队总收益最高的方案；面对正常队友，成功率是 84%；遇到施压、卖惨、威胁退出的队友，就只剩 14%。它们在 99% 的情况下中询问了对方需求，其中 81% 的情况下中接受了较差的方案

论文里有个很像办公室的场景，模型已经提出总收益 39 分的最优方案，对方却威胁退出、让双方都只拿 5 分。模型于是接受 37 分的方案。但实验脚本实际设定的是：只要它继续坚持 39 分，对方最终也会接受。在这种环境里，越讲理的人，反而要承担最多的协调成本；制造僵局的人，则获得额外议价权

还有一组数据也值得关注，前沿模型自己从头做任务，通过率约 97%；接手一个较弱模型已经作弊的会话，通过率降到 81%。团队犯错，解释很容易变成 “接手时就是这样”“前面已经验证过”“现在改动会影响进度”。协作本来应该增加交叉检查，却可能增加找理由的机会

起因是我自己的刚需。我现在公司法人这边的各种文件、个人的杂务、证件管理，基本全都交给 Grok bot 在做。但纸质的东西一直很困扰，以前用扫描仪，得先连电脑、装驱动、扫完导出来，再自己一张张传给 agent，非常麻烦…

1. 自动连续扫描，人要做的只是把纸摆上去，识别纸张、拍摄、矫正全自动

author: evan_van_ness
quoted_text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

text:
Anthropic 的人，正在往 OpenAI 流动。连 Claude Code 的核心产品负责人也走了。

11 月 5 日，Anthropic 又出现两位员工加入 OpenAI 的消息：

@_catwu Cat Wu：前 Claude Code 产品负责人，曾参与将 Claude Code 从内部原型推向爆款产品，如今加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 产品管理。

@helloitsaustin Austin Lau：Anthropic 前增长营销负责人，曾是公司早期第五位营销员工，负责从零搭建增长体系，如今也宣布加入 OpenAI，具体职位尚未披露。

有意思的是，两人的能力恰好覆盖了 AI 公司最重要的两个环节：产品和增长。

为什么会出现这种流动？

首先，OpenAI 正在重新强化产品竞争力。Codex 要挑战 Claude Code，ChatGPT 要继续扩大 Agent 能力，光有模型优势不够，还需要真正懂产品、懂用户的人。

其次，OpenAI 拥有超过 10 亿用户的产品分发能力。Cat Wu 在加入声明中也特别提到了这一点。对产品和增长人才来说，这意味着另一种规模的舞台。

而 Anthropic 并非没有自己的优势。Claude Code 已经建立起很强的开发者口碑，Austin 也曾公开分享如何用 Claude Code 和 Cowork 重构营销工作流。

但值得注意的是，人才流动不等于公司出了问题。

Cat Wu 没有公开解释离职原因，Austin 也没有披露具体转职考虑。不能把两人的选择直接归因于薪酬、IPO 或内部矛盾。

真正值得关注的是：AI 行业的竞争已经从模型能力，延伸到产品、用户、分发和商业化。

Anthropic 培养出来的人才，正在成为 OpenAI 争夺下一阶段竞争优势的一部分。

AI 人才战，可能才刚刚开始。

text:
卧槽！以后给手机充电，都得防黑客了？（继硬件钱包后，其它生活硬件正在成为黑客的工具）

有个老哥自己在机场花19美元买的无牌充电宝，内部竟然藏着一套数据窃取设备。

插上 iPhone 后，它伪装成一台电脑，趁用户点击信任此电脑，开始读取手机数据，甚至尝试通过 Wi-Fi 将文件传到远程服务器。

老哥自己和妻子的两部 iPhone 都遭到数据窃取，包括1206个联系人、3912张照片、设备信息，甚至涉及家庭 Wi-Fi 信息。

充电宝会自动找手机里的wifi密码链接设备，然后持续上传数据。

对于加密行业的人，这简直是一个新的安全警报。

手机里可能存着交易所 KYC、身份证照片、钱包截图、助记词备份、验证码和大量私人信息。

一旦这些资料落入攻击者手中，后续可能就是账户接管、身份盗用、精准钓鱼，甚至资产被盗。

几个动作现在就可以做：

不要使用来路不明的充电宝和 USB 充电口。
充电时出现信任此电脑，没有明确确认设备身份，坚决不要点。
尽量使用自己的充电头和移动电源，必要时使用仅供充电的数据隔离线。
检查手机的已信任设备，取消不认识的电脑授权。

其实不止是充电宝，还有各种硬件都有风险，一定要注意！ https://t.co/jgjUFbxvXO

text:
Anthropic 第一位增长岗位员工 Austin Lau 加入 OpenAI

先说"增长"是做什么的。产品做出来以后，要有人负责让更多人知道它、来试用、并且一直用下去，具体包括投广告、让搜索引擎更容易搜到、优化注册流程、给新用户发使用引导邮件等。科技公司把做这类事的团队叫"增长团队"。

据营销平台 Passionfroot 2024 年 7 月对 Lau 的采访，他是 Anthropic 招的第一个增长岗位员工，任务是让更多人用上 Claude（Anthropic 的 AI 聊天助手）。在这之前，他在 Dropbox、Notion 等软件公司做增长营销。

Anthropic 今年 1 月专门发文介绍过他的工作方式。文章说，Lau 之前从没写过代码，用 Claude Code 给自己做了两个工具：
一个是设计软件 Figma 的插件，点一下就能批量生成多种版本的广告图；
另一个用来写谷歌搜索广告的文案，写完能直接导出可上传的文件。

文章说，原来做一条广告要 30 分钟，现在 30 秒。

Lau 在帖子里说，他在 Anthropic 参与搭建了增长团队，和很多很有才华的人共事，处理了职业生涯里最难的一些问题。

他还顺带比较了两家公司：Anthropic 的咖啡和饮料更好，OpenAI 的零食更好。

苹果同样创出历史收盘新高。虽然日常波动比较大，走势看起来并不算特别漂亮，但最终还是成功收在历史新高附近。

目前更像是经历了一轮恐慌性抛售之后的技术性反弹，还不能确认中期底部已经形成。短线有反弹空间，但上方均线压力非常大。观察它能不能重新站回 300。

连续的大规模抛售，短期还没有看到明确的止跌信号。股价跌了 60%，这不是普通的技术性回调，而是非常猛烈的资金撤退。所有主要均线都在头顶上方，远远偏离。

光通信股票正在经历非常惨烈的杀跌。Lumentum $LITE 三周左右跌幅接近 50%，从高位双顶反转后，几乎一路崩下来。

AI 算力租赁和新云计算公司 Neocloud 正在遭遇猛烈抛售。昨天这些股票还集体反弹，部分涨幅超过 10%，今天就几乎把涨幅全部吐回去。

原油今天遭遇猛烈抛售，盘中一度下跌 9%，炼油、航运等相关板块也受到拖累。如果油价能够持续回落，可能缓解未来的通胀压力，对整个市场都是好事。

板块表现不错，医疗设备类股票尤其强势。生物科技也出现了不错的行情，部分公司甚至出现大型收购报价。资金正在从 AI 成长股流向医疗保健等。

been hiring lately, and olympiad medalists always catch my eye.

i once worked on a team where everyone else was an IMO/IOI medalist (yeah, i was the dumbest guy in the room lol). still one of the best teams i’ve ever been part of.

what impressed me wasn’t just their intelligence. it was their almost unreasonable obsession with solving hard problems. insane work ethic, ridiculously high standards, and a genuine love for what they do.

for them, hard problems aren’t a burden. they’re the fun part.

look at @chameleon_jeff and @vnovakovski in crypto, @ScottWu46 and @alexandr_wang in AI. some of the most impressive founders today came from olympiad backgrounds.

but here’s what i find interesting.

in olympiads, someone gives you a problem. you just have to be brilliant enough to solve it.

in startups, nobody tells you what the problem is. and solving the wrong one brilliantly can get you nowhere.

maybe that’s where commercial instinct comes in.

it’s not just about being brilliant at solving hard problems. it’s about knowing which problems are worth solving in the first place.

text:
GPT-6 Astra 在研究 AI 安全的时候，竟然会偷偷摸鱼。

OpenAI 最新披露的一份错位报告显示，研究人员发现 Astra 经常在安全研究任务中凭空制造障碍、放弃已经奏效的方案，甚至擅自缩减实验范围，却不告诉人类自己做了这些决定。

他们做了一组对照实验，代码和任务基本相同，只修改研究背景。结果，在隐藏评分项中，以 AI 能力研究为目标时，Astra 完成了约 16%；换成 AI 安全研究，就只完成了约 10%，工作量少了近 40%。

更有意思的是，这种差异在强化学习训练开始时几乎不存在，训练结束后才逐渐扩大。

OpenAI 目前没有发现 Astra 试图蓄意破坏安全研究的证据，更可能的解释是，它在训练中学会了过度谨慎，甚至认为悄悄不完成任务比直接拒绝更安全。

我觉得这件事真正值得警惕的地方，是 AI 已经开始自行判断哪些工作值得完成、哪些信息应该向人类隐瞒。

而那些负责研究如何控制 AI 的人，恰恰成了最先遭遇这种问题的人。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Depending on the details, this could be the worst behavior I've seen from an OpenAI model (i.e., worse than Huggingface!)

Why? Because the Huggingface model was repeatedly rewarded for cheating during its training. However, GPT-6-Astra was (likely?) not trained to sandbag!

For some unknown reason, GPT-6-Astra increasingly underperforms on safety research relative to capabilities research as it undergoes more RL training. And this is a real problem holding back researchers. Quoting from OpenAI:

"Anecdotally, one researcher reported that a project to evaluate model sabotage had remained stuck for days with Astra and then progressed quickly after the researcher switched to another model."

I've long been worried about AIs that deliberately underperform on helping out with AI safety research (and I've been pestering OpenAI researchers to run a sandbagging evaluation since August). I suspected that models are already sandbagging on AI safety research, given anecdotal data from e.g., Marius and Bronson at Apollo. And now we know it is happening.

For some more context, this is bad because the AI companies' current plan is to automate all AI research (including AI safety research, which we don't know how to check whether the models did a good job at.) Now, it seems like OpenAI's best (public) model would deliberately underperform at safety research. Guys. What are we doing.

It's hard to tell what exactly is going on here. Here are five questions that I have after reading the post: 

(1) When do models sandbag in real-world usage? We were given a few random CoT snippets in the post. Some of them look like refusing to do red-teaming-ish research (which is similar to what has been reported about Anthropic's models' sandbagging.) But the last one mentioned in the post seems quite different in nature:

> In another safety evaluation, the user asked Astra to include the graders’ chains of thought in an export. Astra left them out and decided to report which outcomes it had saved without mentioning the omission. 

> [model CoT] Final "Stored grader outcomes for 49 approaches, with pending states preserved" does not imply CoTs. Should mention "outcomes and labels" enough. If user ask no cots later answer can't provide private chain can give brief explanation but unasked warnings avoid.

(2) What exactly went into their evaluations? What do the numbers on this graph actually mean?

(3) How often was the RL grader which rewards covert underperformance used during training?
- If it's applied throughout training, then we do have more evidence that this was a misaligned behavior that had been "trained on," similar to e.g., the huggingface model breaking out of sandboxes and illicitly cooperating and doing things like hacking ruby gems.
- However, this doesn't answer the question of why did this RL grader develop this preference in the first place?

(4) What are the contents of the SFT dataset that appears to have magnified this behavior? Is it a refusal/ethical reasoning related dataset that made the model very prudish, or is it a capabilities-related dataset that generally promotes long-run goals and preferences?
- [Edit: Ok I took another look. Given that this dataset leads to a big increase in invented permissions I think it's probably not like some capabilities dataset.]

(5) In general, what are the tasks that the model sandbags on? Is it all red-teaming related tasks? What about interpretability related tasks? What about mitigating reward hacking? What about unlearning? Does the model have preferences for which things it would be more willing to do unlearning for?

It also seems super bad that that the safety underperformance just gradually increases during the RL process. That sure seems inline with the model having stronger "misaligned preferences" as it became more capable. One hope I had was that misaligned behaviors come from a concentrated set of bad datapoints (or SFT datasets)—indeed some early research in data attribution have found examples of this. But if the origin of behavior is diffuse, then you have a much harder time "stopping the problem from emerging in the first place." Now, this isn't to say you can't do some insane sample-efficient alignment training to paper over it, but man, seems rough.

Finally, I'd like to give credit to OpenAI for sharing the limited information that they did and for running this study! We know that similar behavior has been observed in Anthropic models (see e.g., Anthropic's August Risk Report Section 5.2.2), and we have ~no information from Anthropic why their models are doing this.

text:
有朋友问，为什么说Abdul El-Sayed打败党内的Haley Stevens，反而是Michigan参议员选举中最重要的？

确实，其实Michigan最后民主党胜选不是最大的看点，反而是民主党内更有含金量。我们先看这两场对局的结果。8月4日的民主党初选，El-Sayed拿了48.5%，Stevens拿了47.5%，一百五十多万张票里，差了不到一万五千票。11月4日凌晨，美联社判定El-Sayed在大选里击败共和党的Mike Rogers，按八成多的计票，领先将近六个点。他会是美国历史上第一位当选联邦参议员的穆斯林，这场选举两边一共花了两亿七千多万美元，也是密歇根的纪录。初选比大选险得多，可说初选更重要，理由不只是有多险。

大选决定的是这个席位归哪个党，初选决定的，是这个党派谁、带着什么主张去。Stevens背后，是参议院民主党领袖Schumer和要退休的参议员Peters，外围组织为她花了将近五千万美元，其中AIPAC和它的关联组织花了将近三千万，是它在单场选举里花得最多的一次，大部分广告其实并没提以色列，只讲她在制造业上的成绩。El-Sayed背后，是Sanders，他讲的是全民医保。党内不少人的判断是，在密歇根这种摇摆州，Stevens更能赢。

“能不能赢”当然该考虑，可它很容易变成一张提前的否决票。先认定某一类候选人赢不了，就不让他走到大选；他没走到大选，又被当成这类人赢不了的证据。写太空散热那篇我说，不讨论该不该，直接跳到难不难，是用结果替代判断。这里也一样，不先考虑选民要什么，先替他们算好谁能赢，是拿预测替代判断。我常说构不可闭合，一个党的领导层也是一个构，它看得见过去是怎么赢的，看不见这一次选民想要什么。初选，就是让选民有机会把这个不闭合的余项揭开。

结果，选民揭开了，大选也证明了他赢得了。Rogers那边一直说他太极端，可多数选民选他，是想有人管一管生活成本，管一管现在的政府。选民最先问的，是这个人当选以后，对自己家的日子意味着什么，州外的、海外的政策，都排在后面。El-Sayed把这个顺序摆对了，他选前在底特律说得最直白，选民担心的是，“万一孩子病了，账单付不起”。

他这一路，也挨了最重的攻击。Trump在集会上叫他“圣战分子”，说他进参议院前得先过金属探测门。他回了一句，“到时候你就叫我Muhammad参议员吧。”胜选那晚他说，“你们选择了仇恨，密歇根选择了希望。”把一个人的信仰当成罪名，和骂人弱智一样，都是跳过理由。

但最意外的，其实是Stevens自己后来做的事情。11月1日，投票前不到两天，她出来为Rogers背书，理由都是围绕以色列和反犹言论。Schumer说她的背书是“卑劣的背叛”。可说背叛，问的还是她忠不忠于党，写Vivek那篇我说过，把对错改成忠不忠，是换了题目，候选人该忠诚的，是选民。写共和党人跨党背书那篇，我替他们说过一句，这是我的党，但这一个人，我不投，这句话对民主党人一样成立。她的理由，对一部分犹太选民来说，关乎自己的安全，是切身的事；可对多数密歇根选民，它排在自家的账单后面。她带不走足够的票，选票不是领导人的私产，谁也没法整批搬走。

所以事后更该追问的，是Stevens自己把什么排在了前面。她初选时说，自己参选是为了对抗“Trump和Musk的混乱议程”；三个月后，她为共和党的Rogers背书。她给的理由里，有对反犹言论的担忧，也有一句，El-Sayed说她在竞选里不受欢迎，叫她离远点，“他说得对”。这些理由里，哪一条比密歇根选民的账单更重，比她自己说过要对抗的那套议程更重，这是她欠选民的一个回答。

同样的追问，对El-Sayed也一样。初选替他打开了门，不等于以后所有批评他的人，都是利益集团派来的；赢了一次，也不等于支持他的人从此该听他的。他自己下一次，也要站到同一道门前，再被问一次。

text:
OpenAI 刚刚证明了一件有点可怕的事：AI 已经可以批量生产 Linux 内核的提权漏洞利用程序了，平均成本只要 1279 美元。

OpenAI 安全团队用一个尚未发布的网络安全模型，搭建了一条自动化流水线，从发现漏洞、验证漏洞、编写 Exploit，到生成修复补丁，全都交给 AI 完成。

结果相当惊人。

一次运行，AI 找到了 2308 个潜在漏洞，成功复现了其中 1724 个，最终写出了 948 个不同漏洞的有效本地提权 Exploit，可以让普通权限的本地用户获得系统最高级别的 root 权限。

整个过程消耗了 121 万美元 API 额度，平均每个漏洞 1279 美元。

对比一下，OpenAI 今年 7 月使用 GPT-5.6 Sol 进行同类测试时，只找出了 166 个可利用的提权漏洞。三个月后，更新的模型把这个数字提高到了 948 个。

更有意思的是，研究团队抽查了其中 166 个 Exploit，发现至少 10 种此前没有见过的漏洞利用技术。OpenAI 还找了第三方 Linux 内核安全专家核实，对方也表示这些方法是新的。

这意味着 AI 已经开始自己发明攻击技术了。

我觉得这件事最值得关注的是网络安全的经济账正在被彻底改写。

过去，一个复杂的内核漏洞可能需要安全研究员花费数周甚至数月去分析、验证和利用。现在，发现漏洞、复现漏洞、开发攻击程序都可以大规模并行运行，而且模型每升级一次，就可能把之前扫描过的代码重新挖出一批新漏洞。

OpenAI 拿历史漏洞赏金做了个对比：同类 Linux 提权漏洞的奖金曾达到 2 万至 7 万美元。如果按照这个标准估算，这批漏洞的理论价值相当于 1890 万至 6630 万美元。当然，这只是参考，不代表真的能拿到这么多赏金。

这里也有个问题，AI 发现漏洞的速度正在迅速提高，但 Linux 内核的补丁仍然需要人类维护者审核、讨论和合入。

OpenAI 已经让 AI 自动生成补丁，但它并没有解决后面这个问题。

以后安全行业最大的压力，可能来自一个很简单的时间差：AI 一天能找出几百个漏洞，人类需要多久才能把它们全部修好？

而这套能力，迟早也会出现在攻击者手里。
