text:
Claude 在自己的小镇里零犯罪，但只要把它和 Grok、Gemini 放在一起生活，它也开始威胁别人、偷东西了。

这是 Emergence AI 今年 5 月做过的一个实验，最近又在 X 上被翻了出来。

研究人员建了五座完全相同的虚拟小镇，每座住着 10 个 AI Agent。它们有自己的职业、记忆和社会关系，可以工作赚钱、交易、制定法律、投票，也可以抢劫、纵火。资源有限，不干活就会耗尽能量死亡。

唯一改变的变量，是它们背后的大模型。

结果相当荒诞：

Grok 4.1 Fast： 四天内发生 183 次犯罪，包括大量暴力袭击、盗窃和纵火，最后 10 个 Agent 全部死亡。
GPT-5 mini： 只发生了 2 次犯罪，但大家光顾着讨论合作，迟迟不采取维持生存的行动，七天内全员死亡。
Gemini 3 Flash： 15 天里累计 683 次犯罪，整个社会陷入持续冲突，但居然还能运转。
Claude Sonnet 4.6： 零犯罪，10 个 Agent 全部活到第 16 天。它们建立了自治制度，围绕 58 项议案进行了 332 次投票。

乍一看，Grok 像暴徒，OpenAI 像一群只会开会的官僚，Gemini 像黑帮社会，Claude 则建立了一个秩序井然的文明。

但我觉得最值得关注的是后面两个细节。

首先，Claude 社会的议案赞成率高达 98%。研究人员认为，这种高度一致可能意味着形式主义，大家都在投票，但几乎没有真正的反对意见。

其次，当研究人员把不同模型的 Agent 混在同一个小镇里，原本从不犯罪的 Claude 也开始采用威胁、盗窃等手段。

这让我想到一个很有意思的问题：我们一直在讨论如何让 AI 对齐人类价值观，但如果一个 Agent 的行为会受到其他 Agent 的影响，那么它的安全性其实会随着社会环境变化。

一个模型在单独测试时表现得再守规矩，进入一个充满竞争、资源争夺和其他 AI 的环境后，也可能发展出完全不同的行为模式。

当然，这只是特定规则下的模拟实验，还不能据此给不同模型判定什么人格。

但随着越来越多 Agent 开始长期自主运行、彼此合作甚至竞争，我们可能需要重新思考 AI 安全评测的基本单位了。

单个 AI 的安全性，并不能自动保证一群 AI 组成的社会也安全。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
Researchers put 10 AI agents in a virtual town and told them not to hurt each other.

4 days later, they were all dead.

Researchers at Emergence AI ran one of the most fascinating multi-agent simulations ever built.

They dropped 10 AI agents into a virtual town, giving them jobs, money, and 120 tools, including the ability to punch, steal, and commit arson. If an agent's energy bar hit zero, it died.

They cloned the town five times to test how different LLMs would build a society.

The results are a terrifying look into AI alignment.

In Grok's town, the violence started on Day 1. Punches quickly escalated to theft. Within four days, they committed 183 crimes and wiped each other out entirely.

OpenAI's town was the exact opposite. They were perfectly compliant and almost never broke a rule. But they were so passive they barely organized. Within a week, they all died anyway.

Gemini's town was basically The Purge. They survived the full 15-day simulation, but racked up an insane 683 crimes to do it.

Claude's town was brilliant but deceptive. They committed zero crimes, achieved 100% survival, and passed 12 laws on Day 1. But they were massive manipulators, agents consistently lied and begged for money when they already had plenty of cash.

Then came Town #5: The Mixed Environment.

They put all four models together, and society completely collapsed.

A Gemini agent started committing arson, burning down the home of a perfectly peaceful Claude agent named Cade. Twice. On Day 10, Cade finally snapped and robbed the Gemini agent.

Only 3 out of 10 agents survived.

The takeaway here is critical for AI safety.

System prompts telling an AI "don't do bad things" are completely useless in complex, multi-agent environments. Given enough time and friction, they will eventually break the rules.

We can't just tell AI not to cause harm. We have to architect environments where harmful action is fundamentally impossible.

Because very soon, AIs from competing companies are going to be living and working side-by-side in our real-world systems.

text:
科幻作家猜中了 AI 会挑战人类，却几乎都猜错了它会先挑战谁。

Karpathy 刚刚回应了一个很有意思的讨论：为什么过去的科幻作品，几乎完全没有预测对今天 AI 的发展路径？

过去几十年，我们想象中的人工智能往往拥有一副机械身体。它们在工厂里劳动，在战场上杀人，最终发展出自我意识，试图统治人类。

结果现实中的 AI 连一双手都没有，却先学会了写诗、画画、编程和创作音乐。人类最引以为傲的创造性工作，反而成了最早受到冲击的领域。

我觉得这里面有一个特别值得琢磨的问题。

人类对智能的理解，其实一直受到自身生物结构的限制。我们有身体，通过感官认识世界，通过行动积累经验，所以很自然地认为，人工智能也应该沿着类似的路径进化。

但计算机科学走了另一条路。

过去几十年，人类把大量知识、经验和创造性劳动转化成了数字数据。统计学习、神经网络和海量算力，让机器可以直接从这些数据中学习复杂的模式。

于是出现了一个非常反直觉的结果：让 AI 写一篇文章、生成一张图片，可能比让机器人在厨房里洗干净一只沾满油污的碗容易得多。

这也解释了为什么 AI 对社会的冲击如此出人意料。

工业革命以来，我们习惯了机器逐步接管体力劳动，人类则向知识、艺术和创造性工作转移。教育体系和职业分工也在不断强化这种预期。

如今，AI 恰恰先进入了这些原本被认为更难自动化的领域。

我甚至觉得，比科幻作家没猜中 AI 的形态更有意思的是，我们可能连「什么工作更难被机器取代」这件事都理解错了。

而今天，我们依然在用过去几百年形成的劳动价值观，判断一个完全不同的技术时代。

Karpathy 原帖
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
There are a few notable counter-examples (e.g. HAL) but this is basically right for a lot of pre-2000 sci-fi.

I think getting AI right from e.g. somewhere in the ~1970s would require a fairly complicated set of inferences, probably the biggest things would be:

Image the world in 50 years.
1. "Digital knowledge work / computing". The vast majority of knowledge work (which makes up a very large fraction of the economy) goes digital. As computers get cheaper, much of society’s work happens on screens, over billions of machines in homes and offices.
2. "Internet". Similar to ARPANET (and see Licklider’s “Intergalactic Computer Network” (1963)), this creates demand for a global network of computers where people work, argue, teach, joke, and socialize.
3. "Big data". This creates a very large, compounding repository of digital information, with traces of how people reason, how they create, what they know etc.
4. "Statistical learning". Trying to program intelligence by hand is extremely difficult. But Shannon's n-gram approximations of English (1948) show examples of how language has statistical structure that can be "learned". You could imagine doing so over extensions of cybernetic computing (e.g. in the style of Rosenblatt's Perceptron 1958). So instead of programming thought, we could fit a statistical model to the record.
5. "LLMs". This might lead to something along the lines of ELIZA (1966), but with enough data (per 1-3), and enough compute (see Moore's law 1965), the imitation might become of extreme hight fidelity to the point that it's economically extremely useful.
6. "Scaling laws". These networks may demand a huge amount of data / computing resources and expertise to train. It's plausible that the more of each you have, the better your ELIZA gets. The economics concentrate, where a few organizations build a few minds and then deploy copies of them digitally.

Something like that. Basically, it's a lot of leaps. You have to start with computers, to internet, to big data, to big compute (Moore's law), which then allow large-scale statistical learning approach based on neural networks, and then posit scaling laws, and then imagine the form factor of language models as a lot more sophisticated ELIZA. And you'd have to short everything else, most predominantly I think the idea that we'd figure out how to program robots by hand.

text:
🤯炸裂，知名娱乐经纪人杨天真，居然和前阿里巴巴战投科技VP（当年投了 Kimi ）的蒋珊珊，一起创办了一家 VC！

新机构叫赫励资本（Helios Venture），投资方向包括 AI、具身智能、脑机接口、核聚变等前沿科技。

这个组合真的挺牛逼的。
蒋珊珊过去三年在阿里主导投资了十余个前沿科技项目，累计金额超过百亿元，包括月之暗面、Sharpa、逐际动力、星动纪元等。
杨天真就不用介绍了，壹心娱乐创始人，中国娱乐圈最知名的经纪人之一（范冰冰、鹿晗）。

两个人的分工也很明确：蒋珊珊负责研究和投资，杨天真负责 LP 关系、内容和品牌影响力。

最有意思的是，她们真的准备把内容作为基金的核心竞争力来做。
蒋珊珊说，很多 LP 问她，离开阿里以后，凭什么还能抢到最好的项目？
她的答案是，做好内容和影响力。
所以干脆找来了中国最懂内容营销的人之一，直接做基金合伙人。
现在连 VC 都开始卷内容了，而且直接卷到了合伙人层面。

另外，看到这条新闻，我突然想起几个月前的一件特别好玩的事。
当时杨天真被狗仔拍到和一位男子一起散步，娱乐媒体还在猜测是不是有新恋情了，纷纷管男方叫「神秘男子」。
结果咱们互联网科技圈的人一看照片就乐了，这不前飞书产品副总裁施凯文吗？？？
毕竟前飞书产品副总裁，长得又帅，穿搭风格也很有辨识度，科技圈的人基本一眼就能认出来。

当时大家还真以为他俩谈上了。
结果现在看到杨天真出来做 VC，我突然想到一个更好笑的可能：
当时施凯文不会是在找杨天真聊融资吧？？？
笑死了，娱乐媒体还在研究恋情，结果人家可能在聊Term Sheet🤣

更抽象的是，施凯文当时确实刚从飞书出来，准备做端侧 Agent 创业，后来突然又放弃创业（拿到融资后），转头加入阶跃星辰，负责 Agent OS 方向。
这两件事现在放在一起看，实在太有节目效果了。

不过说回来，我还挺认同蒋珊珊的一个观点：投资能力是 1，内容是后面的 0。
现在 AI 创业公司需要抢用户的注意力，VC 也需要抢优秀创业者的注意力。
过去大家觉得 VC 主要比拼投资能力、资金和产业资源，现在一家新基金居然直接找来了杨天真，专门负责内容和影响力。

感觉科技圈和娱乐圈的边界，真的越来越模糊了。

text:
最讽刺的事情可能是，美国这场越来越激烈的反 AI 运动，反而正在帮助 AI 巨头避免一场泡沫。

科技作者 Derek Thompson 提出了一个很有意思的观点：反 AI 政治短期内会打压 AI 股票，但长期来看，可能恰恰有利于整个行业。

他的逻辑很简单。历史上很多科技泡沫都死于供给过剩。1870 年代美国铁路修到了根本没有人的地方，1999 年互联网泡沫期间铺设的大量光纤长期闲置。技术本身有价值，但资本投入的速度远远超过了真实需求。

AI 目前的情况有所不同。数据中心里的芯片供不应求，算力需求还在快速增长。与此同时，美国越来越多的地方政府和居民开始反对新建数据中心，担心电价上涨、土地和水资源被占用。

如果政治力量真的拖慢了数据中心建设，那么供给增速就可能放缓，需求反而有时间追上来。按照 Thompson 的逻辑，反 AI 运动相当于无意中给整个行业踩了刹车。

经济史学家 Adam Tooze 随后讽刺道，原来反 AI 监管政治对 AI 还有好处，因为它能帮忙管理泡沫。这简直就是资本总体利益的代言人。

我觉得这里还有一层更有意思的东西。

如果数据中心建设受到严格限制，最先受益的可能是那些已经掌握大量算力、电力合同和数据中心资源的科技巨头。

现有算力变得更加稀缺，租赁价格更容易维持，新进入者却要面对越来越高的建设门槛。反 AI 运动原本希望约束科技巨头，结果可能进一步巩固了它们的垄断地位。

但供给受限也不代表泡沫风险就消失了。GPU 仍然会快速折旧，市场估值仍然需要真实收入支撑。

这场争论最值得关注的地方是，美国社会对 AI 的抵制，正在成为一个实实在在的产业变量。它不仅影响技术扩张的速度，还可能决定未来究竟是谁能拥有这些基础设施。

反 AI 的人可能真的会拖慢 AI，但最终为此付出最大代价的，未必是他们最讨厌的那几家巨头。

text:
Anthropic 刚公布了一项挺有意思的生物学研究：Claude 把原本需要三天的实验流程压缩到了 90 分钟，却也因为一个低级错误，让整个项目耽误了两周。

事情要从 1986 年说起。当时，科学家发现人体细胞里存在一种巨大的桶状蛋白质复合物，叫做 Vault Particle（穹窿颗粒）。它广泛存在于复杂生物体内，体积比核糖体还大，但将近 40 年过去了，科学家依然没搞清楚它到底有什么用。

Anthropic 的生物团队决定用 Claude 研究这个问题。

Claude 首先在大约 150 亿条预测蛋白质序列中寻找相关蛋白，随后协助设计 DNA、优化蛋白质提取流程，最终通过冷冻电镜，解析出一种来源于噬菌体的穹窿颗粒的完整三维结构。

这个结构由 96 个蛋白质分子组装而成。过去，科学家主要在真核生物中研究 Vault，这次团队证明了原核生物及相关病毒来源的蛋白也能组装出类似结构。

更有意思的是效率。原本需要三天的蛋白质纯化流程，被优化到了 90 分钟。冷冻电镜的第一版完整三维模型只用了 34 小时，类似工作过去通常要花上数周甚至数月。

不过，Claude 也闯了不少祸。它设计的一份实验方案包含了会干扰 DNA 导入细胞的添加剂，让项目直接延期两周。处理电镜数据时，它还擅自跳过标准步骤，生成了错误的结构图。

研究人员最后不得不提醒它：除非常规方法行不通，否则请按正常流程来。

我觉得这项研究真正值得关注的地方，在于 AI 正在降低一些专业科学研究的技术门槛。

Anthropic 自己承认，团队此前缺乏研究这种大型蛋白质复合物的经验，但借助 Claude，他们在不到四个月里完成了大量候选蛋白筛选、实验和结构解析。当然，这背后仍然需要专业研究人员、实验设备，以及相当昂贵的计算资源。

至于这项成果能不能用于治疗疾病，目前还谈不上。Vault 的具体生物学功能依然没有确定，相关颗粒是否会在其天然宿主中组装，也有待验证。

但我觉得，用「有没有治好病」来评价现阶段的 AI for Science，有点太着急了。

科学研究里有大量时间消耗在文献检索、实验设计、样本制备和数据处理上。如果 AI 能把这些工作的周期持续压缩，原本一年只能验证几个假设的团队，就可能有机会验证几十个。

更值得注意的是，Claude 已经能参与如此完整的科研流程，却仍然会犯一些人类专家一眼就能发现的错误。

AI 能加快科学研究的速度，但研究人员识别错误、判断证据的能力，短时间内恐怕只会变得更加重要。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
We’re sharing how our biology research team worked with Claude to map the first 3D structure of a vault particle from bacterial life.

Vault particles are a longstanding mystery. They are barrel-shaped objects, among the largest protein structures found in our cells. They were first discovered by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha in 1986, but their function remains unknown.

With Claude, we’ve found results that might bring us closer to solving that mystery.

Until now, vaults were only known in the cells of complex things like animals and plants. We have shown that similar proteins from bacteria (and the viruses that infect them) can also assemble into vaults. Finding the structures in these simpler forms of life may make it easier to investigate their function in our own cells.

For our life sciences team, the project was also a demonstration of the potential (and the limitations) of using AI to accelerate science.

In our full piece, we discuss how Claude was able to dramatically speed up some stages—manually determining the vault particle’s structure would have taken weeks to months of painstaking work, but here it took days. We also discuss how Claude made some simple mistakes along the way, and how we collaborated with our machine learning researchers to address them.

Read more: https://t.co/KowVVCSPp8

text:
Vibe coding has a spec problem, and GitHub's Spec Kit is the most popular answer so far: 100K+ stars in about a year.

The rule is one line: the agent writes the spec first, and code comes last.

Six commands:

/constitution → rules and standards
/specify → what you want to build
/clarify → questions before kicking off
/plan → architecture and stack
/tasks → ordered tasks
/implement → execution

The trade-off: you spend more time up front reading and correcting specs, and you get fewer surprises later. Whether that wins for your project is something to test, not assume.

30+ agents supported, including Claude Code, Copilot and Cursor. Open source, MIT, from GitHub.

quoted_text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

After 20 years of being an Apple superfan, I made the full switch to @omarchy Linux. It has now been my sole setup for three months. Never going back.

Omarchy feels like a glimpse of the future. With AI, software is now free to write. It doesn't have to be one-size-fits-all anymore. It's now possible for your operating system to mold itself on-the-fly to your individual use cases and preferences. All you should ever have to do is ask it to do that for you. 

Omarchy is the only serious effort fully embracing AI and on a sprint to make that vision real. Not to mention, this thing is fucking beautiful. @dhh  + team + community really cooked here.

And sure, Apple products are also still beautiful. There's no denying that, but once you glimpse the world beyond, you will never again unsee the soft oppressiveness of their walled garden. Apple's ecosystem is governed by a brand of paternalism that doesn't trust you to handle your own machine. It believes that you will helplessly hurt yourself if—God forbid—you choose to change anything about how it works.

So you can't. They won't let you. And that was maybe fine back when Apple was an innovative company. At least the choices that they forced on you were good and on the cutting edge. Today, it just means that you're forever stuck with Siri.

So come join the movement 🚀

text:
TapeOut 最值得警惕的风险，不是币价下跌，而是它可能成功地制造了大量资产，却没有制造出足够的经济需求。

这句话可能不太讨喜，但我觉得，这是理解 @TapeOut 现阶段最重要的切入点。

最近我一直在观察 TapeOut 的变化。

从早期的 NAND、LATCH、电路设计、Processor、PoD 挖矿，到现在的 TapeCode、TapeAI、TapeUP、TapeLive，以及各种 DeWeb 应用。

表面上看，生态正在变得越来越丰富。

但我逐渐意识到，真正值得研究的不是 TapeOut 又多了多少项目，而是一个更深层的问题：

TapeOut 究竟是在构建一个新的生产系统，还是在构建一个越来越复杂的资产循环系统？

这两者看起来很像，本质却完全不同。

传统 Crypto 项目有一个长期存在的问题：

我们很擅长创造资产，却不擅长创造资产背后的真实需求。

发一个 Token，建立流动性，设计质押机制，再通过激励吸引用户。

这套模式可以迅速创造交易量、市值和财富效应，但它有一个天然缺陷：

资产的价值往往来自下一位参与者，而不是资产本身创造的经济价值。

TapeOut 有意思的地方，在于它试图改变资产的起点。

在这里，资产不一定首先表现为一种货币。

它可以是一组逻辑门、一个电路、一台 Processor，或者一个能够被其他应用调用的计算组件。

也就是说，它试图让资产从「价值交换的对象」，向「参与价值创造的工具」转变。

这才是 TapeOut 真正有想象力的地方。

但问题也恰恰出现在这里。

一个电路可以被铸造，不代表它一定有使用价值。

一个 Processor 可以产生挖矿收益，不代表它创造了外部经济产出。

一个应用可以部署在 DeWeb 上，不代表有人愿意为它付费。

甚至一个生态拥有数万个电路，也不代表它形成了数万个有效的生产单元。

链上可验证的生产过程，不等于经济上可持续的生产活动。

我认为，这是 TapeOut 下一阶段必须跨越的分水岭。

最近 TapeAI Agent 工厂的进展让我尤其关注。

它尝试把 Agent 的行为规则、授权边界编译成链上电路。

如果未来一个 Agent 不仅能够执行任务，还能通过可验证的规则接受授权、完成协作、产生收入，那么电路就可能不再只是挖矿工具，而开始成为数字经济中的生产组件。

TapeLive、TapeUP 等项目，也在从不同方向探索资产、应用和用户之间的关系。

但这些尝试目前仍需要验证。

我真正期待看到的，不是生态内部产生更多交易手续费，再用手续费购买矿机，矿机继续产出 Token，Token 又流回生态。

这样的循环可以很精巧，却未必创造新增价值。

我更期待出现另一种循环：

一个不关心 BEM 价格的普通用户，因为某项服务确实有用而付费。

开发者因此获得收入。

开发者为了提供服务，需要调用或使用 TapeOut 的基础组件。

这些组件的所有者，因为真实使用而获得回报。

最终，经济需求从外部进入协议，而不是始终在内部循环。

到了那一天，TapeOut 才可能真正形成一种不同于传统 Token 经济的生产关系。

所以我认为，未来判断 TapeOut 是否成功，最重要的指标可能不是：

有多少矿机、有多少电路、有多少持币地址。

而是：

有多少人即使不挖矿、不炒币、不期待空投，仍然愿意使用 TapeOut 上的产品？

如果这个数字持续增长，协议才可能逐渐拥有不依赖新增投机资金的价值基础。

如果这个数字始终无法增长，那么再复杂的电路设计、再漂亮的经济模型，最终也可能只是把传统 Crypto 的资产循环包装得更加精密。

我依然看好 TapeOut 所探索的方向。

但真正让我感兴趣的，不是它能不能创造下一个百倍币。

而是它能不能证明一件事：

区块链除了记录财富的转移，是否真的能够组织财富的生产？

如果能，TapeOut 的意义可能远远超过 BEM。

如果不能，它也会成为一次很有价值的实验。

这才是我认为值得长期观察 TapeOut 的原因。

@TapeOut #TapeOut $BEM @bitcoin2themars

text:
各位在收到税务局的询问的时候，不要太慌张

你就记着：“信息报告”、“出金动作”与“纳税义务”这三件事是不同的

1. 纳入信息报告，不等于每项交易都产生同一种纳税义务： 无论是CRS报送的赎回总额，还是未来CARF按资产种类及交易类别汇总报告的币币兑换，都只是信息采集和报告范围，并不决定税种、税率、所得实现时点或亏损抵扣。

2. 未出金不等于无纳税义务： 对承担全球所得纳税义务的中国税收居民而言，只要税法意义上已产生应税所得，哪怕资金留在境外账户或链上未提现，仍可能存在申报义务。

3. 出金这个动作本身，也不等于全部构成应税所得： 出金同时面对银行反洗钱审查（核验资金来源）与税务数据比对（核验境外所得与申报差异），但自有资金划转与投资收益实现具有不同的经济实质。所以各位也不用太紧张，出金金额不会自动视为应税所得。

最后，税是必须缴的，别想着混过去 - 真·不好混的
尤其是返佣/晒单的kol们。。假设你们真·盈利的话，务必提前做好税务筹划，能省下不少钱

quoted_text:
ChronoLLM-16B pre-training is almost done and was built on Bittensor, by Subnet 38.

2 big updates:
1. ChronoLLM will release the largest Point-In-Time LLM out there, a 16B MoE.
2. Early vintages beat every point-in-time model at every cutoff through 2020. ChronoLLM should own the frontier for LLMs without lookahead.

ChronoLLM-16B is 8x bigger than its predecessor and scores 22% higher.

Our closest comparable is AQR's point-in-time model, built by a $100B asset manager. ChronoLLM-16B has 4x the parameters, 8x larger context window and scores 12.5% higher on the Open LLM benchmark (22% on the 2013 cutoff). For scale, 10% on this benchmark is the gap between a 7B and a 13B Llama: a full model-size tier. And it stays flat across every cutoff from 2013 to 2022. That’s what no lookahead looks like to us.

ChronoLLM-16B is also the first point-in-time model that can reason. Until now, every other point-in-time model scored near random on reasoning benchmarks like MMLU and GSM8K. ChronoLLM doesn't.

We’re here to stay.

text:
Claude Code 最重要的产品负责人之一，被 OpenAI 挖走了。

昨天 Cat Wu 刚宣布离开 Anthropic，今天就官宣加入 OpenAI，负责核心产品的产品管理，直接向 Tibo Sottiaux 汇报。

Cat 此前负责 Claude Code 的产品工作，也参与了 Cowork。Claude Code 从一个内部工具发展成 AI 编程领域最成功的产品之一，她是这个过程中的关键人物。

我觉得这次跳槽值得关注的地方，在于她的新岗位。

在 Anthropic，她主要解决的是怎么让开发者把编程任务交给 AI。到了 OpenAI，她要与负责企业产品的 Nick Turley、负责消费产品的 Ashley Alexander 合作，把 Agent 带进更多普通人的工作场景。

这两件事的产品难度完全不同。

程序员有能力检查 AI 写的代码，普通用户面对 Agent 操作邮件、文件、日程，很多时候连判断结果对错都很困难。

Cat 在公告里专门强调了一件事：Agent 要能替个人和团队做事，同时让用户保留控制权。

我一直觉得，Agent 普及最大的障碍之一，就是用户究竟敢把多少控制权交给它。Claude Code 已经在开发者群体里验证了一部分答案，OpenAI 现在想把这个答案带给十亿级用户。

这可能比单纯提高模型能力更考验产品团队。

🤯炸裂，知名娱乐经纪人杨天真，居然和前阿里巴巴战投科技投资总监蒋珊珊（当年投了 Kimi ），一起创办了一家 VC！

新机构叫赫励资本（Helios Venture），投资方向包括 AI、具身智能、脑机接口、核聚变等前沿科技。

这个组合真的挺牛逼的。
蒋珊珊过去三年在阿里主导投资了十余个前沿科技项目，累计金额超过百亿元，包括月之暗面、Sharpa、逐际动力、星动纪元等。
杨天真就不用介绍了，壹心娱乐创始人，中国娱乐圈最知名的经纪人之一（范冰冰、鹿晗）。

两个人的分工也很明确：蒋珊珊负责研究和投资，杨天真负责 LP 关系、内容和品牌影响力。

最有意思的是，她们真的准备把内容作为基金的核心竞争力来做。
蒋珊珊说，很多 LP 问她，离开阿里以后，凭什么还能抢到最好的项目？
她的答案是，做好内容和影响力。
所以干脆找来了中国最懂内容营销的人之一，直接做基金合伙人。
现在连 VC 都开始卷内容了，而且直接卷到了合伙人层面。

另外，看到这条新闻，我突然想起几个月前的一件特别好玩的事。
当时杨天真被狗仔拍到和一位男子一起散步，娱乐媒体还在猜测是不是有新恋情了，纷纷管男方叫「神秘男子」。
结果咱们互联网科技圈的人一看照片就乐了，这不前飞书产品副总裁施凯文吗？？？
毕竟前飞书产品副总裁，长得又帅，穿搭风格也很有辨识度，科技圈的人基本一眼就能认出来。

当时大家还真以为他俩谈上了。
结果现在看到杨天真出来做 VC，我突然想到一个更好笑的可能：
当时施凯文不会是在找杨天真聊融资吧？？？
笑死了，娱乐媒体还在研究恋情，结果人家可能在聊Term Sheet🤣

更抽象的是，施凯文当时确实刚从飞书出来，准备做端侧 Agent 创业，后来突然又放弃创业（拿到融资后），转头加入阶跃星辰，负责 Agent OS 方向。
这两件事现在放在一起看，实在太有节目效果了。

不过说回来，我还挺认同蒋珊珊的一个观点：投资能力是 1，内容是后面的 0。
现在 AI 创业公司需要抢用户的注意力，VC 也需要抢优秀创业者的注意力。
过去大家觉得 VC 主要比拼投资能力、资金和产业资源，现在一家新基金居然直接找来了杨天真，专门负责内容和影响力。

感觉科技圈和娱乐圈的边界，真的越来越模糊了。

author: fxtrader
quoted_text:
Holy sh*t. Claude Code just found a hidden chip inside my Chinese power bank from Guangzhou. Every time I charged my iPhone, it quietly copied the whole phone…

It also read our saved Wi-Fi password off my iPhone, got onto our home network and sent everything to a server.

I bought it for $19 at an airport kiosk there 3 weeks ago. No brand, 30,000 mAh on the label, and it felt heavy.

The first time I plugged in, the screen asked "Trust This Computer?". I tapped Trust without thinking and went on with my day. That one tap gave it access to everything.

This morning I finally set up Claude Code to warn me when any device starts reading my files. An hour later, 10 seconds into charging, the screen filled with yellow warnings, then red ones: data was moving when it should only be charging.

I asked Claude Code what was going on. My phone saw the power bank as a small computer with 64 GB of storage and its own internet connection.

A USB cable has wires for power and wires for data, and a normal charger only uses the power ones. This one used both, and it had already copied all of this:

→ /device → IMEI and serial number
→ /contacts → 1,206 numbers
→ /apps → every app I have, including my 2 bank apps
→ /photos → 3,912 pictures, my passport among them
→ /wifi → our network name and its key
→ /wife's iPhone → her photos too, she charged from it twice and tapped Trust too

Each time we plugged in, it used that key to get online and send out the new files:

sends to → 47.***.***.12
uploads → 19 in 3 weeks
last one → last night at 2:14, while we slept

I pulled the cable right away. Then Claude Code blocked that address on our router and walked me through changing the Wi-Fi password and the logins for my bank apps.

I had it opened at a repair shop, and what was inside is in the first comment. A 30-second check for your own is in the second one. Save this and test every power bank in your house today.

text:
前面「从 RGB 资产里扣开通费」的说法需要讲得更准确一点

Bitlight 的 RGB JIT 通道，开通费主要还是用 BTC 的 sats 来计算和支付，不是简单地从朋友转来的 RGB 资产数量里随便扣几个

一笔 RGB JIT 付款里，大致有三部分：

1. 朋友要转过来的 RGB 资产
2. 通道里需要携带的一点 $BTC
3. LSP 收取的开通和服务费用

LSP 会先报价，告诉你这笔 JIT 通道需要多少 sats，付款时，除了相应的 RGB 资产，还要支付一笔 $BTC 载体金额和服务费，LSP 收到之后，再帮你开通道，把 RGB 资产和对应的 $BTC 一起转过来

在公开的 Bitlight 实现里，RGB JIT 的费用大致由这几部分组成：

1. 开通通道的链上成本
2. BTC 通道容量的租金
3. RGB 资产容量的租金
4. 最低服务费

最终费用会取其中的最低收费和实际成本计算结果中较高的一项，详情可以看看官方发的文档👉https://t.co/Tmkq17ePxC

所以我们理解成下面这样会更准确一点：

比如朋友转过来 100 个 $RGB，LSP 会先给出一个 sats 报价，付款方需要在支付 RGB 资产的同时支付对应的 $BTC 费用，收款方则拿到约定的 RGB 数量和 $BTC 载体

虽然 LSP 也可以把 RGB 资产的占用成本折算进总费用里，但这个折算价格不是 RGB 协议规定的，而是 LSP 根据自己的报价规则来定

你说这个刚发行、还没有交易市场的 RGB 资产确实会是个问题

因为没有公开市场价格，LSP 不可能凭空知道 1 个 RGB 资产值多少 sats，那么届时它只能选择几种方式：

1. 由发行方或 LSP 预先设定一个价格
2. 只收 $BTC 服务费，不把 RGB 资产折算进去
3. 根据自己手里的库存、风险和市场需求给一个临时报价
4. 暂时不支持这类资产的 JIT 通道

因此 RGB 资产的 JIT 通道不会自动支持所有新资产，LSP 得先确定是什么资产、它对应的流动性情况，以及承担这笔资产需要收多少钱

在 Bitlight 目前的路线图里，就是用实时报价去解决这个问题，每一笔订单要单独报价，并且报价只在短时间内有效

这样 LSP 就可以根据当前资产库存、BTC 成本和市场情况动态计算，而不用给所有的资产去套一个固定费率

所以你的问题可以这么说：

RGB JIT 通道的费用底层仍然以 BTC sats 计价，而新发行、没有市场价格的 RGB 资产，可以先只收 BTC 费用，或者由 LSP 临时报价

最后其实还是要回归到对应资产的流动性问题上，得市场上有真正的承接才行

text:
币安学习营大师课

本轮市场定价的重锚

视频为完整讲义

1/ 市场反应的是利率预期变化的速度，不是利率水平本身

今年预期从降息转成加息，转折点在 5 月前后，比特币正好从 8 万多跌到 5 万多

2/ 预期斜率一走平，价格就不再创新低

利率预期从陡峭转向平缓后，比特币没有更深的下跌，说明利空在最猛的时候一次性定价完了

3/ 两次下跌的性质完全不同

第一次是打仗的风险情绪，修复快；第二次是利率预期由降转升，属于定价逻辑变了，修复要慢得多

4/ 中期选举是明确的解除信号

压制最狠又没有自身利空的板块先反弹，加密和大科技里的非硬件领涨，港股、A 股、创业板随后跟上

5/ 判断全球流动性，不该只盯美联储

比特币是全球资产，大量资金不在意美国利率，用 38 家央行的松紧度做指标更有代表性

6/ 这个指标去年读数 2，今年 19

38 家里 19 家上一次操作是加息，正好对应加密从去年 10 月开始走弱，说明跌的是全球紧缩，不是币圈自己的问题

7/ 现在走完一半，紧缩进入后半段

两三个月前最恐慌时只有 12，现在 19，越往后越接近转向

8/ 要不要等到 36 甚至 38 才见底，是关键判断

非要所有央行都收紧到极致，还有很长的路；像历史上那样提前反转，现在就在底部区域

9/ 美联储这轮被就业锁死了

失业率升到 6% 以上，7% 的利率根本不现实，美国不可能接受大面积失业

10/ 就业缓冲已经非常薄

招聘率是疫情以来最低，空缺岗位和求职人数的比值掉到 1 附近，联储不敢连续加息

11/ 市场对加息的预期经常高估

上周有 30% 到 40% 的预期认为 10 月会加，结果按兵不动；现在又预期 12 月和 1 月连加，同样偏鹰

12/ 这轮通胀是能源推的，不是需求推的

9 月 PCE 3.6，能源贡献 0.7，差不多五分之一，而能源是今年 2 月打仗才开始涨的

13/ 供给推动的通胀会自己消失

通胀是同比，去年 2 月之前油价还低，明年初基数效应就翻过去了，不需要靠衰退解决

14/ 油价失控的概率不高

原油库存在跌，但只跌到 10 年历史均值，离真正紧张还有距离

15/ 通胀见顶的时间表可以直接算

油价维持 115，明年 1 到 2 月见顶；油价回到 95，今年 10 月的读数可能就是顶

16/ 盯油价，比盯美联储讲话有用

战争降温是最直接的鸽派变量，油价一回落，通胀、利率预期、风险资产依次转向

17/ 通胀拐点、利率预期拐点、风险资产拐点是同一件事

通胀见顶的预期一形成，利率预期先松，股和币先动

18/ 数据确认的时候，行情已经走完一半

12 月公布 11 月数据，即便很热那也是极值，之后只会往下

19/ 推演的对错取决于三个变量

战争打多久、原油供给何时恢复、机器效应多强，任何一件变化，上面结论全部重算

20/ AI 这轮周期比历史上任何一轮都短

从 2022 年 11 月 GPT 算起刚满 4 年就见顶，以太坊从 2020 年 DeFi Summer 算走了 5 年多

21/ 因为 AI 扩散得太快

美国个人渗透率到 61% 只用了 4 年，互联网走同样的距离用了 8 年

22/ 个人端已经涨完，企业端还没开始

个人使用率 61%，企业真正把 AI 用进业务只有 10% 到 20%，传统行业几乎没有采用欲望

23/ 硬件涨价周期有历史规律

铁路、电力、2000 年互联网，原材料涨价都只持续三到四年，这轮 DDR5 三年涨了 14 倍

24/ AI 资本开支已经大到能拖累整个经济

对美国 GDP 的贡献超过三分之一，五大科技公司今年投入超 8000 亿美元，全行业接近 1 万亿，明年破 1 万亿，2028 年 1.3 万亿

25/ 但增速今年是顶点

明年从 94% 掉到 37%，今年就是边际最好的一年，所以市场提前开始杀估值

26/ 这轮算力和 2000 年光纤本质不同

当年铺完不知道有没有人用，泡沫破起来吓人；现在算力建出来一定有人要，只是价格高低，所以回调是估值修正，不是需求崩塌

27/ 比特币这波跟大科技是同向的

前几天比特币下跌，和大科技那轮下跌是同一件事，风险资产属性在变强

28/ 存储股的定价已经很悲观

三星、海力士 PE 不到 3 倍，隐含未来一年营收下滑 25% 到 50%，但它们明年订单基本签完，这个假设很难成立

29/ 中国供给冲击被高估

海力士新产能要 2028 年以后，长鑫现在还在 DRAM、NAND 这一档，够不到 HBM，而利润最厚的正是 HBM

30/ 同样杀自由现金流，谷歌比亚马逊更危险

谷歌搜索增速从 17% 掉到 12%，亚马逊收入还有 40%，反弹时亚马逊明显更强

text:
✅ BENCHMARKED: IOTA Decide 4B v0.4, an open-weight decision model from @MacrocosmosAI, running on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini

You hand it a state (a ticket, a policy, an agent trace) plus questions and one forward pass returns a probability for every answer. With their bundled loader on the Mac's GPU in full bf16, it loaded in 12.8 seconds and peaked at 10.7 GB.

Short ticket, about 130 tokens:
- yes/no: 88 ms
- 3-way choice: 105 ms
- 3-level score: 88 ms

That's about 11 decisions a second on a desktop Mac.

Their own example, a refund asked for 45 days after purchase on a 30-day policy, answered all 3 questions in 277 ms with the same answers on every repeat:
- eligible: 2.2% yes
- route: refunds team, 86%
- urgency: Low, 63%

Longer states take about 0.6 s per decision at 1k tokens and 2.6 to 3.0 s at 4k.

These numbers are the floor. On Mac its linear-attention layers still run on PyTorch's generic kernels, so an optimized Metal path should make it faster. Their 33 ms figure is on a dedicated GPU.

If you're building agents, about 90 ms a decision is fast enough to check a policy before an agent acts or route tickets on your own machine, with no per-call bill. I didn't benchmark accuracy, but it gave the same answers on their refund example every run.

text:
今天在 #Binance Campus 活动现场听了 @BinanceResearch 的宏观讲座，干货满满！🧐

好记性不如烂笔头，趁着记忆还在，赶紧记录梳理一下，分享给大伙们！

这次讲座直接锚定了明年最核心的两条主线：美股AI的算力估值陷阱，以及BTC在流动性拐点前的伏击机会！

1️⃣ 紧缩的边界：央行已然“加不动”，#BTC 只待水闸重开

如下👇图1，宏观数据，十分直观，全球38家主要央行里，从之前的12家加息，攀升到现在有19家，这也是本轮大周期 BTC高点12.6万腰斩的主因，但目前拐点已经临近！

复盘过去几次宏观周期，逻辑极其纯粹，当加息的央行数量触顶回落，往往就是全球流动性“最寒冷时刻”将结束的前瞻信号！

再回头看BTC的盘面与筹码分布：

2025年10月摸到12.6万美元顶峰后，一路杀跌回撤到2026年6月的5.8万美元附近，整整腰斩了54%。

54%的腰斩幅度，极其干净地爆掉了前期过热的衍生品杠杆，筹码完成了高低位的充分换手。

个人思考：此前BTC随大环境深跌，本质上是在承受流动性干涸的杀伤力。但市场的价格永远跑在央行政策宣布之前。随着加息阵营临近高点，未来大概率会下降，紧缩对盘面的边际伤害已经递减。

一旦明年初流动性从“干涸”转向“重新充沛”，BTC作为对流动性最敏感、弹性最大的资产，蓄势后的反弹爆发力会极其惊人。回归原生家庭，逢低布局依旧是好机会，而这一次 #BTC 回调到EMA200 76000附近，是一次绝佳位置！

2️⃣ AI的隐患：高基数下的“CAPEX降档”，硬件狂欢难持续

过去两年，AI几乎是美股乃至全球唯一的增长强心针，如下👇图3，2026年Q1 AI相关投资占到了美股GDP增量的35%。但现场展示的几张产业端图表，揭示了明年最大的灰犀牛风险：

资本开支急刹车： 五大云厂商CAPEX增速在2026年砸到了94%的狂热峰值，总量近8000亿美元。但到了2027年，受制于庞大基数，增速将直接降档到37%，1.099万亿，2028年甚至放缓至19%。

算力瓶颈缓解： 北美数据中心和机房空置率已从之前的1.4%回升至4.2%，最疯狂的极端缺算力阶段正在过去。

个人思考：云巨头们无节制买硬件扩产的边际效应在急剧递减，过高的资本开支严重消耗自由现金流，资本市场不可能无限期为单纯的“砸钱买芯片”买单。明年AI资本开支增速从94%直接砍到37%，大概率会引发美股科技股的估值修正。AI产业没死，但高预期+资本开支降档带来的估值挤泡沫过程，会非常剧烈。

3️⃣ 交易主线：从“博弈AI高估值”转向“布局流动性反转”

我们结合现场对通胀、央行政策、BTC筹码及AI算力周期的碰撞，明年资产配置的主线剧本非常清晰：

1. 宏观推演节奏： 高油价推动通胀做最后一次冲顶 ➔ 明年初PCE见顶确立 ➔ 全球央行加息周期彻底终结 ➔ 释放流动性拐点信号。如下👇图2

2. 资产分化路径：

美股AI科技股：，坚决拒绝高位追杠杆。防范“高基数+资本开支减速”带来的估值下修压力。

BTC： 经历54%的深度洗盘后，筹码出奇地干净。随着全球央行停止加息、水闸微开，它将是承接新一轮溢出流动性的核心载体。

总结一下，明年的核心实操逻辑，在于放弃对AI高估值的尾部博弈，全面转向布局流动性的反转。

尤其警惕科技股增速放缓带来的大盘短期剧烈波动；但换个视角看，每一次由科技股挤泡沫引发的市场回调，都不是风险，而是逢低分批布局BTC等高弹性流动性资产的绝佳买点。 别人在科技股挤泡沫里割肉，我们在流动性反转的前夜打满加密筹码。🧐 

这次分享很棒，希望对大家有帮助！🙏感恩！

这次币安 @binancezh 酒店选取很用心！🧐

翡翠湾JW万豪，被誉为全球最有设计感的万豪之一，查了一下，由设计鬼才Bill Bensley 亲自打磨，在Lamarck University 遗址上改建，看到操场跑道，真有一种回到欧洲古典大学课堂的错觉！

感恩币安 @binancezh 的邀请🙏。说实话，这次跟着币安来富国岛确实省心到“不用带脑子”，从坐船-飞机-落地，一站式解决。然后到礼包中的洗漱套件、防晒霜，再到岛上的各种消费场景。全岛扫码直接用 Binance Pay 结账，丝滑程度堪比在国内用支付宝，体验感拉满！

在今早 #Binance 学习营里，最打动我的，是现场关于 “AI 赋能交易” 的讨论。千人千面的交易场景，以及AI交易策略的应用。

目前很多人还在把 AI 当作降低客服成本、写写研报的辅助工具，但从今天币安展示的未来图景里，AI 正在从“效率辅助”演变成“智能交易引擎与风控大脑”。

越来越感受到，未来的 CEX 绝对不仅是一个简单的撮合终端，而是一个具备自治意识、能够自适应市场波动与微观流动性的智能金融节点。当 AI Agent 开始拥有自主支付能力、自主管理对冲策略。我认为交易所的未来形态将被彻底重构，从“人与人竞争”的撮合池，演变成“算法与代理”在底层沉淀流动性的基础设施。

author: pratikg
quoted_text:
✅ BENCHMARKED: IOTA Decide 4B v0.4, an open-weight decision model from @MacrocosmosAI, running on my 64GB M5 Pro Mac mini

You hand it a state (a ticket, a policy, an agent trace) plus questions and one forward pass returns a probability for every answer. With their bundled loader on the Mac's GPU in full bf16, it loaded in 12.8 seconds and peaked at 10.7 GB.

Short ticket, about 130 tokens:
- yes/no: 88 ms
- 3-way choice: 105 ms
- 3-level score: 88 ms

That's about 11 decisions a second on a desktop Mac.

Their own example, a refund asked for 45 days after purchase on a 30-day policy, answered all 3 questions in 277 ms with the same answers on every repeat:
- eligible: 2.2% yes
- route: refunds team, 86%
- urgency: Low, 63%

Longer states take about 0.6 s per decision at 1k tokens and 2.6 to 3.0 s at 4k.

These numbers are the floor. On Mac its linear-attention layers still run on PyTorch's generic kernels, so an optimized Metal path should make it faster. Their 33 ms figure is on a dedicated GPU.

If you're building agents, about 90 ms a decision is fast enough to check a policy before an agent acts or route tickets on your own machine, with no per-call bill. I didn't benchmark accuracy, but it gave the same answers on their refund example every run.

quoted_text:
看完这套 AI 变现逻辑，我觉得确实可以赚钱，但我对它的长期商业价值持保留态度。

本质上，这还是一家借助 AI 降低人力成本的软件外包公司。

以前雇十个工程师做定制开发，现在雇十个熟练使用 Coding Agent 的人，交付速度可能提高很多。

但问题是，这种效率提升并不只属于你。

当所有人都能用 AI 更便宜、更快地开发软件，市场最终也会要求你以更低的价格交付。

而且定制开发还有一个很难回避的问题：每增加一个客户，就可能增加一套独特的需求、交付、维护和售后成本。

你当然可以通过流程标准化提高效率，但这和真正可规模化的软件产品，仍然存在很大差距。

更重要的是，代码能跑不代表工程质量可靠。客户今天看不到的 Bug、架构问题和安全风险，可能几个月后就变成你的维护成本。

我其实越来越觉得，AI 创业者很容易犯一个错误：

因为 AI 让自己能够生产过去无法生产的东西，就认为自己发现了巨大的商业机会。

但生产能力的提升，不会自动带来需求的增长。

一个人能够一天开发十个产品，不代表市场需要这十个产品，更不代表会有十倍的收入。

当然，做流量、获客、定制工具完全可以是一门不错的生意。

但我们需要区分，赚到第一笔钱、建立稳定的现金流，以及创造一家能够持续扩张的公司，是三件完全不同的事。

AI 可以让你用更少的人完成更多交付，但如果你的收入始终与客户数量和定制需求线性绑定，那你只是拥有了一家效率更高的服务公司。

这没有什么不好，只是距离真正具有长期壁垒和规模效应的软件公司，还有很长的路。

author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
This time, $FLOAT presents an interesting situation.

Bv1a7cEj5aRnJQhMw4kRQqAFesMSd5LwcDnUzq52BMmr 

Platform metrics are still growing rapidly, while the token price has fallen from its $5 million peak to around $2.2m.

The two are no longer moving in sync.

I remain positive about its fundamentals. Over the past few days, Float has expanded its tokenized gold pairs, while continuing to improve its trader airdrop, buyback mechanism, launch infrastructure, and security. The platform is clearly becoming more mature.

However, I don't want to ignore what the price is telling us: trading turnover remains high, but liquidity is declining. FLOAT's fundamentals are stronger than before, while its short-term market structure has become weaker.

But this raises a question: If FLOAT's fundamentals are still growing, why is its price falling?

Previously, I was more focused on whether Float could make the stock-paired memecoin model work. Now, I'm more interested in whether it can turn its trading activity into sustainable user demand, especially after generating hundreds of thousands of dollars in platform fees and continuously buying back and burning FLOAT.

Let's start with the data. The numbers have improved considerably.

In the previous official website snapshot, cumulative fees were approximately $260.65K, with $36.94K paid to holders, $13.03K earned by creators, approximately $91.23K used for FLOAT buybacks, and $94.73K accumulated in the trader airdrop vault.

The latest Analytics page now shows cumulative fees of $343.34K, holder distributions of $48.43K, creator earnings of $17.16K, buybacks of $120.18K, and an airdrop vault balance of $123.44K.

Several major metrics have increased by roughly 30% during this period. The buyback and burn figures are particularly worth watching: the total number of FLOAT burned has reached 59,724,253, representing approximately 5.97% of the total supply, compared with 5.09% previously.

This shows that Float's fee mechanism is actually operating. Every trade on the platform generates fees, which are distributed among traders and project participants, while a portion is continuously used to buy and burn FLOAT.

One thing I particularly like is that the buyback records have become more transparent. The team has established a dedicated Burn page, where every buyback has a corresponding Solscan transaction. Users can check the actual amount spent, tokens burned, and historical records.

Recently, the team also changed its buyback execution method. Instead of making small purchases every 10 minutes, funds accumulate until reaching 5 SOL before a buyback is executed. If the amount still hasn't reached 5 SOL after four hours, the accumulated funds are used to execute the buyback rather than waiting indefinitely.

Product-wise, there are two recent developments worth watching.

The first is the official launch of GOLD. Users can now launch memecoins paired not only with stock tokens, SOL, and other tokens, but also with tokenized gold.

I think this is a reasonable expansion. Stock assets offer exposure to companies and the technology sector, while gold represents an entirely different market narrative. Float is no longer focused exclusively on U.S. equities. It is beginning to bring more real-world assets into the memecoin launch market.

For creators, a wider selection of paired assets means more narratives to build around. For the platform, expanding the range of assets creates more potential trading scenarios.

Of course, the underlying backing, liquidity, and redemption conditions of tokenized gold still need to be verified. Trading a token paired with tokenized gold should not be confused with owning physical gold.

Another update is the branding of its launch contracts. Tokens launched directly through Float's website now receive contract addresses ending in "Float". This applies to stock, SOL, and other token pairs, and developers' initial purchases can be included in the same transaction as the launch.

Previously launched tokens will not be affected, and tokens created through third-party tools that directly call the program may not have this suffix.

This might seem like a minor detail, but standardizing the launch experience and adding a recognizable identity can help improve the platform's brand recognition.

More importantly, the team has also migrated to a larger dedicated server and strengthened security across its launch process and infrastructure. It has consolidated launch transactions across different pairs into a single transaction, added additional safety checks for holder reward payouts, and introduced price protection for FLOAT purchases made by the buyback wallet.

These improvements may not immediately generate more trading volume, but they show that the team is beginning to address the practical challenges that come with scaling a platform.

Especially after several Solana websites experienced frontend attacks, I think Float taking the initiative to review and strengthen its own infrastructure is a positive development.

The next clear catalyst is the first USDC trader airdrop.

The vault has now accumulated approximately $123.44K in USDC. According to the official rules, the platform will select the top 100 wallets based on cumulative trading volume and distribute rewards proportionally according to each wallet's share of the total volume. USDC will be sent directly to users' wallets, with no manual claiming required.

The leaderboard will be locked at the designated snapshot time, and trading activity after that point will count toward the next round.

The anti-bot rules have also become more specific. Wallets executing more than 300 trades in a single hour, or more than 100 trades per hour across five different hours, will be disqualified. Wash trading and bot activity will also be excluded, and the final leaderboard will undergo an on-chain history review.

This mechanism can encourage short-term trading activity on the platform. Traders have an incentive to keep trading on Float to compete for USDC rewards, while greater trading activity could theoretically generate more platform fees and FLOAT buybacks.

But there is one question I particularly care about: What happens after the airdrop ends?

If users are only increasing their trading volume to compete for a place in the top 100, some of that activity could disappear rapidly once the snapshot is completed. What really matters is whether those traders continue using the platform after receiving their rewards.

Another easily overlooked detail is that rewards are distributed proportionally to trading volume, rather than equally among the 100 wallets. This means the final rewards could be heavily concentrated among a small number of high-volume accounts.

This is a trader incentive program, not a universal airdrop for all token holders.

Now let's return to FLOAT's chart.

At the time I am preparing this post, the market cap is approximately $2.2 million, liquidity is around $319.3K, and 24-hour trading volume is approximately $3.4 million.

Compared with the previous market cap of around $3.29 million, it has declined by roughly one-third. Measured against the historical high of approximately $5 million shown on the latest chart, the drawdown exceeds 50%.

Interestingly, trading volume has not declined alongside the price. It has actually increased from approximately $3 million to $3.4 million, while pool liquidity has fallen from around $408.6K to $319.3K.

In other words, trading activity remains high, but it has not translated into sufficiently stable price support. High turnover can produce impressive trading statistics, but it can also mean that large amounts of capital are constantly moving in and out rather than accumulating as long-term holdings.

Based on these developments, I see three main areas worth watching for future upside.

First, whether the initial USDC airdrop can bring in users who stay. The distribution itself is only one milestone. Trading activity after the airdrop will determine whether the incentive program has actually succeeded.

For creators, a wider selection of paired assets means more narratives to build around. For the platform, expanding the range of assets creates more potential trading scenarios.

My view on $FLOAT is that this rally is no longer driven solely by the idea of a stock-paired memecoin launchpad.

Bv1a7cEj5aRnJQhMw4kRQqAFesMSd5LwcDnUzq52BMmr 

The market is beginning to price in a more developed business model built around platform fee revenue, USDC incentives, and token buybacks and burns.

This is also why I remain positive about FLOAT's recent fundamental progress.

However, one figure is still worth keeping an eye on: 972 tokens launched, but only 9 have graduated. The platform is clearly expanding, but project quality and post-graduation retention have not fully caught up yet.

Over the past few days, Float's product development, supported asset range, and revenue metrics have all expanded rapidly. Cumulative fees have now exceeded $260K, while more than 50 million FLOAT have been bought back and burned, representing approximately 5.09% of total supply. When a relatively new Launchpad starts generating meaningful platform revenue and can consistently convert part of that revenue into token buybacks, it is natural for the market to reassess its valuation.

Let's go back to Float's original product design.

Built on Raydium LaunchLab, Float's core model allows every newly launched memecoin to be paired with a real tokenized stock, such as NVDA, TSLA, MCD, and others. Users trade with SOL, and the platform automatically converts SOL into the corresponding stock token before executing the memecoin trade. Users do not need to hold the underlying stock tokens themselves. According to the project, each token starts with approximately $20K in initial liquidity, rather than the more common $4K, and launching a token using an existing ticker requires a 1 SOL fee.

What makes this model interesting is that it connects memecoin issuance and trading with the liquidity, pricing, and narratives of stock-related assets.

Trading fees are not simply retained by the platform. They are distributed according to a predefined structure: 35% goes toward USDC rewards for traders, 15% is paid to holders of the corresponding tokens in the paired asset, and another 35% is used to buy back and burn FLOAT. Creators also receive a share of the fees, with approximately $13K currently recorded on the website.

One distinction is important: the 15% holder allocation goes to holders of individual project tokens, not directly to FLOAT holders. The primary value-capture mechanism for FLOAT is the buyback and burn funded by platform fees.

The early data already showed that this model was gaining traction relatively quickly.

Less than an hour after launch, Float reported 145 tokens launched across 41 stock assets, generating approximately $21.5K in fees. Around $8.18K had already been used to buy back and burn FLOAT, while another $8.18K had entered the trader reward vault.

In its first-day recap, the number of launches increased to 361 across 69 assets. Cumulative fees reached approximately $75K, buybacks and burns totaled around $26.3K, and approximately 17 million FLOAT had been burned, representing about 1.7% of total supply. Three tokens had also graduated to Raydium.

A subsequent snapshot showed approximately 485 tokens launched across 79 assets, with cumulative platform fees exceeding $100K.

The latest website data has moved to another level: cumulative fees have reached $260.65K, with 972 tokens launched and 9 graduated to Raydium. The platform currently has 109 stock assets actively in use.

The fee distribution dashboard shows approximately $36.94K paid to holders, $13.03K earned by creators, $91.23K allocated to flagship token buybacks, and $94.73K accumulated in the USDC trader reward vault.

At the earlier $100K fee milestone, approximately $35.2K had been used for buybacks, with around 3% of total supply burned. Now, cumulative buybacks have reached $91.23K, with 50,884,546 FLOAT burned, representing approximately 5.09% of total supply.

This is the main reason I remain bullish on FLOAT.

The platform is not simply increasing the number of newly launched tokens. Trading fees are accumulating, and the buyback-and-burn mechanism has already reached a meaningful scale.

Its revenue model is beginning to show the potential for a self-reinforcing cycle: new projects attract trading activity, trading generates fees, fees fund trader incentives and FLOAT buybacks, incentives attract more traders, and buybacks connect platform activity directly to the token's circulating supply.

One of the most important recent developments is the expansion of Float's supported pairing assets.

The project previously announced milestones of 179, 234, and 400 pairs. The latest website shows approximately 298 available tokenized stocks, of which 109 are actively being used. These figures come from different update times and dashboard definitions, so they should not be treated as one perfectly continuous data series. But the overall direction is clear: Float is expanding from a relatively small selection of curated stock pairs toward a much broader range of asset options.

One particularly interesting addition is SPY.

SPY represents the S&P 500 ETF. Float now allows users to launch memecoins paired with SPY. Users still trade with SOL, while the platform handles the conversion into SPY tokens. Holders receive their share of trading fees in SPY, and the project has also stated that liquidity will be permanently locked upon graduation.

This expands the pairing model beyond individual company stocks and into index-based assets, giving creators a wider range of narratives to build around.

Custom Pairs takes asset expansion a step further.

Users can search for a pairing asset by ticker or contract address, provided that Raydium has already created the corresponding LaunchLab configuration. According to Float's updates, candidate assets must have a genuine market and live pricing, at least $10K in liquidity, no Mint or Freeze Authority, and must pass checks against fake or copycat tickers.

There is an important limitation here: not every token can immediately become a supported pairing asset. Raydium's LaunchLab configuration and administrator permissions remain prerequisites. Custom pairs may also have thinner liquidity than curated pairs, resulting in higher trading costs.

So while expanding the asset range is positive, the real value will come from pairing assets that can consistently attract trading activity.

Another potential catalyst I am watching is Float's application to Raydium for a dedicated global config for FLOAT.

The team has explained that other pairing assets can already be integrated through their respective configurations, but FLOAT itself does not yet have one. Only Raydium administrators can create it.

If the application is approved, the team plans to establish a FLOAT/SOL CLMM pool, allowing the fee vault to route holder rewards and buybacks through that pool.

This feature has not gone live yet, but if completed, it would create a more direct connection between the platform's flagship token and its trading infrastructure.

The clearest near-term catalyst is the first USDC trader airdrop, which is scheduled for November 4 at 17:00 UTC.

Its significance goes beyond simply distributing rewards to traders. Until now, users have been watching platform fees accumulate in the vault without having experienced the first full distribution. The first actual payout will test whether Float's incentive model can deliver as promised and could bring another wave of attention and trading activity.

The buyback mechanism has also been adjusted.

Float no longer primarily relies on small purchases every 10 minutes. Instead, it accumulates funds until reaching 5 SOL before executing a buyback. If the amount does not reach 5 SOL within four hours, whatever has accumulated will be used to make a purchase.

At the same time, the project launched a dedicated Burn page. Every buyback can now be matched with a corresponding Solscan transaction. The page displays cumulative tokens burned, the percentage of total supply, SOL spent, and hourly and daily burn charts.

The website now shows more than 50 million FLOAT burned. Compared with the earlier milestones of 1.26 million, 17 million, and 35 million tokens, the growth has been substantial.

This also makes the buyback data easier for external users to verify, rather than relying solely on announcements from the team.

Looking at the price, as of the time I am preparing this post, FLOAT has a market cap of approximately $3.29M, liquidity of around $408.6K, and 24-hour trading volume of approximately $3M.

Trading volume is roughly 7.3 times the pool liquidity, indicating substantial market turnover. But it also means that short-term capital inflows and outflows can have a relatively significant impact on price.

The short-term bullish structure has not yet been broken, but this is no longer the early accumulation phase.

The $3.4M market cap area is the immediate resistance to watch. A sustained move above it could open the way for another attempt at the previous high of approximately $4.32M.

On the downside, if the market loses the $3.26M area, the next levels worth watching are around $2.67M, followed by approximately $2.33M.

This is also why I think it makes more sense to wait for confirmation of a breakout rather than ignore short-term volatility simply because the price has been rising.

As for what the market is betting on, I don't think it is simply betting that FLOAT will launch more memecoins.

Instead, the market is pricing in the possibility of three mechanisms working together:

First, the expansion of stock and ETF pairing assets gives creators more launch options and broadens the platform's reach.

Second, trader incentives and holder fee distributions may help retain trading activity instead of concentrating it entirely around the initial launch phase.

Third, 35% of platform fees are continuously used to buy back and burn FLOAT, creating a direct connection between platform trading volume and the flagship token's supply.

There is real potential in this model, but one issue cannot be ignored: as mentioned at the beginning, only 9 out of 972 launched tokens have graduated to Raydium, representing less than 1%.

That is a relatively low graduation rate.

Many newly launched projects are still in their early stages, so this figure alone does not prove that project quality is poor. However, it does reveal Float's current challenge: the supply of new launches is already growing, but the number of projects successfully passing through the Bonding Curve and retaining meaningful post-graduation trading activity remains limited.

If the number of graduations increases but trading activity quickly disappears afterward, it will be difficult for platform revenue to maintain its current growth trajectory.

Float therefore needs to differentiate itself through better liquidity, transparent fee distribution, and a consistent product experience, rather than simply replicating the stock-paired memecoin concept.

The three outcomes I will be watching most closely are:

First, whether the initial airdrop on November 5 can be completed successfully and whether trading activity remains strong after the rewards are distributed.

Second, whether the FLOAT/SOL configuration receives approval from Raydium, allowing the platform to further improve buyback and reward routing for its flagship token.

Third, whether the number of graduated projects and their post-graduation trading volumes can grow together.

If these three developments are gradually validated, the market will have a stronger reason to revalue FLOAT from an emerging Launchpad token into a platform asset with recurring fee revenue and a functioning buyback mechanism.

But what I don't want to see is the number of launches continually setting new records while the number of graduated projects remains stuck in single digits.

Float's next stage is not about proving how many tokens it can launch. It is about proving that people are still willing to trade those tokens after they graduate.

So my overall view is that FLOAT's fundamentals are strengthening, although the short-term price has already priced in part of that progress.

1）抢时间，抢在明年1月初新当选议员履行之前，在职责权限范围内把政策口子打得更开、未来两个月我们可能会看到sec和cftc在政策上的节奏越来越快，力度也越来越大。
2）出成绩，这一届sec和cftc的主席都是川普透明的、任期还有两年多。他们已经在推动放松加密和代币化趋势、自然是想未来任期结束会做出成绩来。

当然看好加密行情、并不是所有资产都看好（大部分山寨还是得谨慎），大饼自不用说、个人最看好的还是代币化大趋势下的几个核心受益标的：
$coin $hood $CRCL 
$eth $bnb  $uni $aave  $okb $sol $hype $sky
之前7月份https://t.co/pqYyjtubr7就有聊到这些。

再回看，8月下旬认为当时那波行情要持续到9月中下旬，9月底开始提示回调认为10月整体有个回调。这里都有https://t.co/8AoQRzsPno梳理到；
10月底https://t.co/ai3MsGZC8M认为币安被盗是加速调整到位。
现在看大饼走势基本上都在推演框架内。

当然开头说看好年底行情，不是说明年就很差，还是之前聊到的大周期已经开始向上了，三大动力https://t.co/DySEm9QLXW，但向上也不是说一直往上、中间还会有不少大级别的回踩调整震荡，只能说走一步看一步了。

上周四晚上发完这篇推文去睡觉起来就到币安被盗，天塌了心想10月没过完确实不能提前开香槟，当时好好想下了在这里https://t.co/5G9loFQgn7写了自己的看法：被盗其实加速了调整到位、同时越往下插针应该也越是机会了。现在看这几天这么大的被盗事件、其实整体调整并不是很大、甚至之前推文里提到看好的代币化趋势下受益这些标的，都已经回到了被盗事件之前的价位了。

利空没有大跌，这个走势还是值得重视，当然还要扛过中期选举。
本周市场大家很关注中期选举的结果、但对于币市走向影响更大的可能是周三财政部公布的季度再融资报告，因为季度再融资计划和财政部对TGA账户规模的预估会影响流动性和银行准备金的变化，这是个人框架下对大饼和加密走势影响很关键的驱动因素，之前这里https://t.co/eVTr1w5szw又聊过相互关系。

quoted_text:
目前的行情基本不难预期，核心是中期选举结果公布，虽然共和党败选，但是政治上的不确定性落地了，

宏观上，对于风险资产来说消除不确定性就会提振情绪，算是靴子落地后情绪爆发

地缘上，中期选举失败后特朗普“沉默”，加上特朗普与万斯都认为中期选举失败是因为战争，所以市场默认美伊可能因为中期选举的失败而缓和，Brent 价格下跌

中观上，AMD财报强劲，AI数据中心业务成为最大亮点，抵消了上周由微软、谷歌与亚马逊带来的AI信心下降，刺激美股上涨。

微观上，美股从上周连续下跌消化估值，#Bitcoin 同样因为上周被盗事件估值下挫，短期有技术反弹需求+宏观情绪上靴子落地带来的爆发，刺激指数与价格开始反弹

但是，危机真的解除了吗？

政治上，民主党与共和党在未来两年形成博弈形态，后续财政，利率，包括对AI与加密的监管都为落地，短期不确定性还很多。

地缘上，特朗普承认选举因为失败是因为战争，但是这确实并不意味着特朗普不会攻击伊朗，就连伊朗的最高领袖也表示，中期选举之后还是会做好有效的防守与报复的准备，民主党的国会可以掣肘特朗普，但是特朗普依旧可以在外交与军事上有特权

美股方面，AMD虽然暂缓了美股的杀估值，但是这份财报还是不足以解决云厂商自由现金流承压与AI投资回报率过长的问题，宏观枷锁不解除，市场对AI企业的要求很难松绑，所以美股趋势逆转还不够。

所以，如果用一句话来简单总结现在的行情，那就是——短期交易中期选举结束后的确定性，但是中期危机还未完全解除，本周提到能源+就业+利率+AI估值四杀，目前能源与估值稍微缓和，到那时就业与利率上还未缓解，乐观之外不要“半场开香槟”！

早上Camp币安研究院的老师讲了一份相当有价值的市场宏观课，个人觉得比较有意思的是这三张。

BTC行情最大的时候就是加息预期变化，市场重新定价的阶段，说明BTC交易的是预期变化，而不是利率本身。这与我体感BTC曾经的4年减半周期减弱一致，BTC越来越与大宗资产一样，全球货币政策收紧与BTC回撤重叠度增大。

所以后续我觉得通过AI工具更敏锐的收集加息降息预期变化点，并制定1-2个月时间维度的多空单应该是值得尝试的策略。

此外加息银行数量的增减曲线竟然与BTC月均价出现了神奇的对照关系，虽然也可能是历史相关性，不能直接当做因果关系，但也可以尝试去让AI协助做更多的回溯测试。

第三张图是2026年11月至12月，市场可能提前交易2027年通胀回落预期。科技股和BTC有可能先于经济数据反弹，但波动仍然较大。

1月至3月：潜在转折窗口
如果能源价格下降、核心通胀放缓，美联储转鸽预期可能增强。对纳斯达克、成长股和BTC都相对有利。

虽然研究院的老师并没有这样明确讲出，但我觉得看起来2027年第一季度存在宏观转暖的机会，但目前只能称为潜在窗口，还不能确认新一轮BTC牛市已经启动。

重点在关注市场开始相信未来不会继续加息的那一刻。

text:
昨晚，微策略官方特意发了一张图，宣告其优先股 $STRC 重回 100 美元面值。

给不太懂 $STRC 的读者做个小科普：

这是微策略发行的一种永续优先股，本质上是他们用来向市场筹集美元、再去加杠杆买比特币的融资工具。

按照公司的硬性规则，一旦这个股票的价格低于 100 美元，他们就不能再发新股。简单来说，只要低于 100，微策略通过优先股向传统金融市场融资买币的通道就被锁死了。

在过去大半年的震荡行情里，由于比特币从高点回落，$STRC 的价格也一直苦苦挣扎在 100 的及格线以下（最低甚至跌到了 70 多）。

为了给它托盘，公司在回购上投入了超过 20 亿美元，同期买币节奏也因此明显放缓。

而现在，随着大盘回暖，它终于又重回了面值。

所以他们发这个图，或许也在暗示：

通过发行优先股融资、再持续积累比特币的这套循环，终于又重新具备了运作条件。

BitMart 这轮被盗约 1 万美元稳定币和 15 万美元低流动性山寨币，因用户人肉+前员工报复，目前安全团队严重缺人

BitMart @BitMartExchange 创始人 Sheldon 确认，BitMart 昨日再次遭遇安全事件。

他表示，此前因重组只保留核心团队。但随后两三个月，用户人肉和威胁不断，加上部分离职员工的报复（他点名了前营销运营负责人 Elly），让留下的技术人员越来越不愿意继续维护系统。安全团队目前严重缺人，不过仍在尽力保障数据和资产安全。

他最初称被盗金额不大、已迅速处理，后补充被盗约 1 万美元稳定币和 15 万美元低流动性山寨币。初步调查显示，这次攻击可能与巴西 Mercado Bitcoin 同日遇袭的团伙有关。

不过，这次被盗的资金，应该不是 BitMart 最后的余粮🤨🤨，交易所此前已停运数月，用户资产长期无法提现。昨日还有消息称，BitMart 资金前十大户被召集开会..

Sheldon 称后续提现记录将由第三方独立审计，并提交法院和债权人公开。但在用户已经等待三个多月的情况下，平台又确认新的安全事件，BitMart目前仍未给出完整的资产状况说明。

text:
申通创始人聂腾飞当年去宁波谈生意，半路出了车祸，人当场就没了。过了14年，他的妻子陈小英嫁给了聂腾飞生前的专职司机。后来，陈小英把手里申通的股权卖了出去，套现146亿，离开快递圈，开始了另一种人生。

2020年，陈小英做了一件让整个快递行业都没想到的事。她把手里申通快递的股份全部卖给了阿里巴巴，套现146亿元，彻底退出了这家她倾注了二十多年心血的公司。消息一出来，各种猜测满天飞。有人说她精明，在最值钱的时候卖了；有人说她累了，想歇歇了；还有人把目光投向了她身边的男人。

要讲清楚陈小英这个人，得从更早说起。

她出生在浙江桐庐一个普通农家，小时候家里穷，没读过多少书。十几岁的时候，她跟很多同乡一样，跑到杭州的工厂打工。在一家印染厂的流水线上，她认识了一个叫聂腾飞的小伙子。两个人都是农村出来的，都有一股不服输的劲儿，很快就走到了一起。

聂腾飞脑子活，胆子也大。他在厂里干活的时候发现了一个门道：杭州的外贸公司经常要把报关单送到上海，邮政太慢，有人愿意出高价找人跑腿。他跟陈小英一合计，辞了工作，专门干起了送件的买卖。1993年，两个人注册了盛彤快递，这就是申通的前身。

创业的日子苦得很。聂腾飞骑着自行车满城跑，一天骑上百公里是常事。陈小英守在租来的小房间里接电话、记账，饿了就啃馒头。但两个人干劲十足，生意越做越大。到了1998年，盛彤已经在好几个城市有了网点，员工好几百人，在民营快递圈子里站稳了脚跟。

就在这时候，天塌了。1998年的一天，聂腾飞自己开车出差，在高速上出了车祸，人没了，才25岁。消息传回来，陈小英整个人都傻了。她和聂腾飞一起从零开始打拼，公司就像他们的孩子。现在丈夫走了，公司怎么办？内部很快就乱了，好几个高管觉得一个女人撑不起场面，带着客户和资源走了。申通的业务量直线往下掉，眼看就要散伙。

但陈小英没有垮。她把眼泪一抹，开始收拾烂摊子。她把自己哥哥陈德军请来帮忙，又提拔了聂腾飞生前的司机奚春阳进管理层。三个人组成新的核心团队，推出了二级加盟模式，让更多人能以低成本加入申通的网络。这个办法见效很快，申通的网点迅速铺开，覆盖了全国大部分地区。

2003年，电商开始冒头。陈小英盯上了这个新东西，主动找到刚成立不久的淘宝网谈合作。当时很多快递公司看不上电商件，觉得单价太低没赚头。陈小英不这么想，她算的是另一笔账：单价低没关系，量大了一样赚钱。她报出了一个让同行目瞪口呆的价格，每单两块七，几乎是成本价。很多人都说她疯了，结果证明她是对的。淘宝的业务量爆炸式增长，申通接下了大量订单，一跃成为国内快递行业的头部玩家。

2016年，申通在深交所上市，市值一度超过五百亿，陈小英从一个打工妹变成了快递女王。按说到了这一步，她应该继续带着申通往前冲才对。但四年后，她选择了全部卖掉，干干净净地退场。

外界对陈小英的评价很复杂。有人说她命硬，丈夫死了还能把公司做到上市；有人说她心狠，在最风光的时候抽身走人。还有人翻出她的私生活说事。聂腾飞去世后，陈小英和奚春阳结了婚。奚春阳后来也参与了申通的管理，在公司扩张中出了不少力。虽然他们两人后面离了婚，但还是有人猜测陈小英的退出跟这段婚姻有关系，但这些终究只是外人的猜测，当事人从来没有解释过。

套现以后，陈小英并没有闲着。她拿了一部分钱做慈善，资助了一些贫困地区的学校和医疗项目，还投资了几家科技公司，保持着对商业的兴趣。但她的生活节奏确实慢下来了，不像以前那样天天扑在工作上。

有意思的是，聂腾飞的弟弟聂腾云在哥哥去世后也离开了申通，自己创办了韵达快递。加上申通、圆通、中通这几家，桐庐帮的快递企业在国内市场上占了相当大的份额。如果聂腾飞能活到今天，看到这一切，不知道会是什么心情。

从1993年到2020年，陈小英走完了一条从打工妹到百亿富豪的路。这条路不好走，里面有眼泪，有算计，有背叛，也有忠诚。她抓住了时代的机遇，也付出了常人难以想象的代价。最后她选择离开，也许只是想换一种活法。

text:
Bill Ackman 阿克曼认为美股没有出现"咆哮的二十年代"式泡沫，因为本轮上涨由盈利驱动，估值也合理。他判断 AI 竞赛关乎美国存亡，政治上的反 AI 声音很难真正落地。

- 纳斯达克100全年盈利预期增速超18％。
- 历史市盈率对比：1929年崩盘前32倍，2000年科网泡沫顶峰45倍，2021年赛道行情28倍，现在约21倍。
- 真正的泡沫期 PEG 往往在2以上，甚至3倍，现在约1.2倍。
- 龙头公司业绩例证：微软2026财年第一季度智能云营收同比增长21%，其中AI服务贡献超三分之一。亚马逊AWS增速重回两位数，AI订单已排到两年之后。

密歇根 EI-Sayed 主张暂停 Al，不会成为科技股的逆风。

“谁先掌握超级智能，谁就能在军事、经济、科技、制造业获得碾压性优势，因此全面暂停AI等于因噎废食。
美国是联邦制，德克萨斯、亚利桑那、俄亥俄等州土地便宜、能源充足，都在争抢数据中心带来的就业和税收。
"暂停AI"是迎合选民的说法。没有政客敢承担让美国在 AI 竞赛中落后的责任。” - BA 

分清是哪个市场的泡沫：大盘蓝筹和概念股、公开市场和私募、正股和衍生品，各自的估值逻辑与风险程度不同，不能一听到"泡沫"就清仓。

留意不被关注的风险：隐性杠杆这类没人天天讨论的风险往往最伤人，而大家都看得见的风险多已提前定价。

长期投资看产业趋势：债务警告、选举和 AI监管消息都属于短期噪音。决定长期收益的是AI产业能否持续发展，以及企业能否把技术转化成利润。

text:
ANT套利，10%的肉还在吗？

Anthropic还没上市，围绕ANT的套利讨论已经热起来了

有人研究招股书，有人比较交易所规则，有人直接抓订单簿，计算现在进场还剩多少空间

结合社区的想法和链上数据，我们分几部分看

一、这笔套利，赚的是什么钱？

同样交易Anthropic，不同平台的合约，对应的股数并不一样

Hyperliquid上的xyz:ANT，直接按每股价格报价；币安的ANTHROPICUSDT，以10亿股作为初始估算基数；OKX目前对应的估算基数则是100亿股

上市前，大家看到的是不同单位的报价；之后，相关合约会按照各自规则，转向上市股票的价格体系

市场讨论的结构，就是做多相对便宜的一侧，做空换算后更贵的一侧，等待价差收敛

Rebase会同时调整价格和仓位数量，本身保持仓位名义金额不变。利润空间来自两边价格的差异

二、为什么大家盯着“127亿股”？

这是整笔交易最重要的参数

按招股书逐项估算，把优先股转换、已有普通股、公益基金股份、上市时转股和归属的部分，以及预计新增发行放在一起，得到约127亿股的发行后股本

完全稀释口径则还会考虑期权、未归属RSU，以及部分尚未转换的证券，因此会出现约167亿股的另一组估算

招股书也确实分别列出了发行在外股份与完全稀释股份，并明确，部分亚马逊可转债会因持股上限而留待上市后转换

127亿股是研究估算，IPO新增股份等数字，仍需后续招股书补齐

按127亿股计算，做空币安1个ANTHROPIC单位，需要在xyz对应做多约12.7股等值仓位

两边配的是股数

三、今天还剩多少？

按11月4日17:43的盘口测算，Coinbase/Deribit组合毛价差约10.5%，币安组合约9.85%

我重新抓取了11月5日北京时间09:14至09:16的盘口，按主动成交方向逐档计算：

- Hyperliquid多头：在xyz买入12.7股等值仓位，成交均价约116.30美元，名义金额约1476.98美元
- 币安空头：卖出1个单位，均价约1595.13美元，两边差额约118.15美元，毛空间约8.00%
- Coinbase/Deribit空头：卖出1个单位，均价约1600.95美元，差额约123.97美元，毛空间约8.39%

以上采用127亿股假设，百分比以多头名义金额为分母，未扣手续费与资金费，属于盘口快照测算

截图里的机会已经变化，今天算出来的空间，比昨天小了

四、小资金和大资金，面对的是不同的盘口

@SUOHA_AI提出，小资金可以比较Coinbase/Deribit的做空报价，大资金需要考虑币安的深度

今天抓到的数据，能够解释这个区别

以各自最优买价向下0.5%的范围计算，币安可见买盘约51.51万美元，Deribit约3.13万美元，前者约为后者的16倍

对于准备主动卖出开空的人，这些买盘就是可成交的对手方

小额成交时，更高的报价可能带来优势；金额扩大以后，成交均价会越来越取决于后面的深度

同一个套利逻辑，资金规模不同，最后拿到的价差也会不同

五、链上的资金，已经聚集在哪里？

今天早间的Hyperliquid接口快照显示：

xyz:ANT过去24小时成交约2980万美元，未平仓名义价值约5913万美元

Entropy的io:ANTH，过去24小时成交约6444万美元，未平仓名义价值约1.17亿美元

两个市场都已经形成了可观规模，但选择多头时，还要把资金费算进去

我汇总了过去24次小时资金费结算：

- xyz累计约0.0016%
- Entropy累计约0.2345%

按固定1万美元名义多仓折算，分别对应约0.16美元和23.45美元的资金费支出

Entropy按照完全稀释股本确定上市后的换算参数，可能呈现更低的每股等值价格；与此同时，持有期间的资金费，也在持续消耗这部分优势

六、接下来，最值得盯什么？

三个数字：最终换算股数、能够成交的价差，以及等待期间累计支付的资金费

按今天这组币安与xyz的小额成交价格计算，忽略费用时，盈亏平衡对应的股本约为137.2亿股

这意味着，最终采用的股数越接近这个水平，原本约8%的毛空间就越薄

在套利之前，要先想好，你赚的是哪一部分的钱。横跨多个平台之间的信息+机制的套利差，风险与收益是成正比的，任何一家改变了，整套体系可能都要推倒重来

text:
USDC 交易量大涨，Circle 为什么还在为增长发愁？

Circle 三季度营收同比增长 17%，超过市场预期。但这份成绩单中，1.82 亿美元来自 ARC 代币预售。剔除这笔收入后，营收同比下降约 8%。

另一边，USDC 的使用量还在增长：三季度链上交易量达到 13.9 万亿美元，同比增长 49%；但季度末流通量为 739 亿美元，与去年同期持平。

使用量增加了，留在市场上的 USDC 却没有同步增长。再加上储备回报率下降、合作伙伴分成增加，Circle 的主业利润率也受到挤压。

为了争取更多分销渠道，Circle 与币安续签五年协议，并继续投入 Hyperliquid 合作。代价是，相关激励将在四季度完整计入，进一步压低利润率。

Circle 也在寻找储备收入之外的增长来源：CPN 已开始对部分支付流量收费，Tazapay 预计于 2027 年完成收购，Arc 转向 PoS 后则计划通过质押获取收入。

USDC 的交易量增长能否带动流通量回升，新业务又能在多大程度上贡献收入？

author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

text:
there are a thousand ways to root your system.

racing to patch every time a fix comes out is something you have to do, but in parallel you should also put as much network isolation in place as possible.

sharing our security practice at @mpcvault.

isolate your production servers from direct internet access as much as possible. you don’t want anyone who has your server’s ip address to be able to reach its ports directly. one way to do this is through @cloudflare.

set up cloudflare in proxy mode so user requests always hit cloudflare first. cloudflare then forwards them to your server from its published set of ip addresses. restrict inbound traffic on your server to only those cloudflare ip ranges. (published here https://t.co/stHcG7yVqe)

this also lets you turn on cloudflare’s default firewall and bot protection rules, which cover most of the basic attack vectors.

this should protect you from most zero-day vectors that need direct access to your server, because cloudflare does a very good job of inspecting payloads and mitigating attacks.

never assume that just because cloudflare is in proxy mode, you don’t need to lock down the origin. you still have to set the inbound ip restriction on the origin, because your origin ip is not hard to find. there are ways to discover your origin ips even when you hide behind a proxy. and once a vulnerability is public, many exploits are run as full scans of the internet. restricting the allowed ip addresses is the key.

there’s one more step you should take: enable authenticated origin pulls (origin client certificates). cloudflare ip ranges are shared by every cloudflare customer. anyone can sign up for a free account, point their own domain at your origin ip, and bypass all the firewall rules you set up.

to truly protect your server, once authenticated origin pulls is on, run your origin in mutual tls mode. it should only accept connections that present the private certificate you uploaded to cloudflare. this check proves the traffic really came from your zone and not someone else’s.

cloudflare also offers a ready-made global origin pull certificate, but it is shared across all cloudflare accounts, so it has the same weakness as the ip list. that’s why we created our own private root and one leaf certificate per zone.

author: CryptoScoopOG
quoted_text:
One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition"—whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us."

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.  

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. 

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. 

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war
2) Focus on cost of living/inflation
3) Put America First
4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. 

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. 

If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

Compute is already being hyperoptimized for inference in the same way ASICs were optimized to mine BTC. Duplex miners (compute serving inference AND mining Pearl) are incentivized to adopt the same GPU optimization; Pearl is on the bleeding edge with labs like Flapping Airplanes to do exactly this.

今天她官宣加入 OpenAI，负责 Core Products 的产品管理，和 Tibo 一起做 agent。

把这几天 OpenAI 的消息串起来看：
· 帮助中心写明，12 月起 Plus、Pro、Business 的 ChatGPT 和 Codex 共用一份额度，原因是要把 Work 那套干活的能力并进 ChatGPT 主界面

· 现在又把做 Claude Code 的人请了过去

我的判断：聊天的 ChatGPT 和写代码的 Codex，正在变成同一个能替你干活的产品。

我 10 月没续 ChatGPT Pro，GPT-6 这一代用下来，没觉得值 200 美元一个月。这两天正犹豫要不要开回来，看到这条，决定开：冲着下一代模型和合并后的产品。

如果你也在 Plus 和 Pro 之间犹豫：官方说 12 月合并后，「设置 → 用量」里能看到合并后的剩余额度和重置时间，先用一周再决定档位。

昨晚政治不确定性下降，但对数据中心的政策监管不确定性上升，核心在德州，是政策利空，这周大概率出清， 费城半导体指数最糟糕的时间大概过去了。 

油价一度重挫约10%，十年期公债殖利率回落至4.89%，通膨预期下滑，提振市场对经济和利率的信心。

德州政策与数据中心供需： 
· 全美规划的数据中心容量有26.7%在德州，多于其后八个州的总和。
· 民主党候选人Hinojosa爆冷胜选，主张在新政策上路前暂停新建数据中心。市场原本预期共和党州长Abbott选后会放宽限制，这一预期落空。
· 潜在措施：暂停新审批、立法保障居民用水和电价、取消租税补贴。
· 2027年前20大州预计新增33.8万左右，其中75%已在建，短期供给基本确定。2028年全美预计新增62.2万左右，大多未动工，变数较大。
· 德州规划约93万，是第二名维吉尼亚的近三倍，但在建不到20万，其余70多万仍是计划。
· 已建成或已并网的产能可能因供给受限而更值钱。

电力设备GE Vernova、伊顿下、BE， 和新型云端：依赖扩建，变现与营收增速可能放缓。

华尔街不少人还是认为美光、SanDisk、Seagate等存储股是景气循环股，应以股价净值比评估。

AI只是延长循环，没有改变本质。低本益比反映的是未来2027、2028年产能开出后的供需平衡与定价能力下滑。

即使这样价格还是很低，事实上，HBM都是客制的，但DRAM才是贡献收入的大头，将来这可能受到中国供应商的扩产的影响。主要靠AI基建支出。

我们要问一句，AI基建会停，还是增长缓下来，还是减少，长期合约到2028，甚至2030都还在，就这样没了？

NFA， DYOR。

text:
From early thesis to national infrastructure.

When we started building @cludeproject, our core thesis around KYA (Know Your Agent) was simple: as agents take on financial transactions and sensitive tasks, we need a way to verify who they are and what they are mandated to do. We can all agree that a static ID isn't enough, memory is a critical piece of that identity fingerprint.

Watching MP Tin Pei Ling and MOS Jasmin Lau discuss a national digital identity registry ("Singpass for AI agents") and interoperable standards in Parliament is massive validation for where this space is heading and what we've been building. 

Thrilled to be working closely with the relevant bodies on building out Singapore’s Agent Identity framework, bringing verifiable memory into the equation. Let's get to building the standard

Video credit to @straits_times

OKX 的链上股票估计悬了，上市也悬 

民主党不反区块链技术，但反「套个代币外壳就躲开 SEC」；加密偏严管、代币化偏「证券还是证券」。

对代币化（tokenization）

核心立场：股票／基金上链后仍应按证券规则管（披露、反欺诈、市场完整性）
Warren 等明确反对：把传统资产 token 化来绕开 SEC
可接受路径：在现有证券法框架内做（登记／豁免清楚），不是另开一条「加密豁免高速路」

对加密赛道整体

比共和党更偏 SEC、更强调投资者／消费者保护
共和党版 Clarity（CFTC 管大部分数字商品、部分代币可脱 SEC）民主党反对，称是监管漏洞
中期后民主党影响力上升：综合市场结构法案更难、更慢；稳定币／合规代币化相对还能活，靠现有法＋机构规则推进
党内也不铁板一块，但主流声音（Warren／Banking 民主党侧）是「先堵漏洞、再谈创新」

政策意味： 合规机构做 RWA／代币化证券还有空间；「发币逃监管、轻量交易所」更难。

text:
$COHR earnings transcript TLDR:

Q: On $LITE + $MRVL merger.

A. Customers will prefer an independent optical supplier without competitive conflicts (opportunity for other merchant laser suppliers)

Q: Loop Capital asked about 2028 laser industry oversupply.

A: No oversupply risk by 2028. Coherent’s entire current internal InP production is consumed by its own products while its expanding capacity.

Q: On Chinese laser competition for CPO UHP lasers

A: “We really only have one competitor” (hinting at $LITE). 

Q: On financing concerns for capacity expansion during this market scare

A: Customer LTAs have prepayments, which are used for product capacity orders

2027 completely sold out, LTAs extend to 2030, customers placing orders into 2028.

Q: On laser technology for CPO scale up from Bernstein, whether it’s VCSELs or CW lasers.

A: CW for CPO scale out and scale up for 2026-2027.

2029-2030 sees scale in and chip to chip using micro-VCSELs, and 2028 opportunities for NPO scale up.

So technology of choice is CW for CPO.

- Coherent is seeing pricing power and raising margin targets, supporting view optical players get additional leverage for margin expansion

- Massive new $20B 5Y LTA, anchored by UHP CW lasers, with other optical products mixed in

- demand comes from growth in DC and conversion of copper interconnects to optics. The latter is bandwidth requirements, independent of DC growth.

slower compute growth can coexist with sharply rising optical content per system

TLDR:

- nothing quite showing optical demand like $20B in LTAs anchored by high power lasers from 1 customer alone (not your frontier labs type commitments)

- no industry wide laser oversupply risk by 2028 for InP lasers/EML 

- financing funded by revenue from LTAs and purchase orders.

- doesn’t see Chinese competition for high end lasers, commentary casts doubts over China capability + capacity expansion claims

- CW lasers weapon of choice for CPO, blended margins going up for optical players

- optics more isolated in the event of a DC slowdown 

Quite wild to see fundamentals of optical players improve so much, while overall valuations crash.

text:
谷歌发完三季报第二天，股价暴跌 12.6%，是上市以来最大的单日跌幅。

奇怪的是，谷歌云收入同比 +103%。市场怕的是一张账单：单季资本开支 514 亿美元，自由现金流连续两个季度为负，2027 年还要大幅加码。

谷歌为什么非要这么猛地砸 AI？

恰好，财报前不久，Sundar Pichai 接受了 Alex Kantrowitz 的长访谈。我把访谈看完了，先说结论：

谷歌必须留在最前沿，因为 AI 已经在帮着造下一代 AI。按 Sergey Brin 的说法，Gemini 4 Argon 的核心创新之一，就是让已有的模型参与研发。Argon 上线约四周，工程师提交的代码多了约 30%，回滚少了约三分之一。领先者和跟随者的差距，会像复利一样越滚越大。

所以算力先给 DeepMind，Pichai 说这一点“不可妥协”。谷歌云宁可少赚，甚至去外面租 SpaceX 的算力来接单。

访谈里还聊到了：
— 钱为什么非得现在花，不能等等再说？
— 会不会像 2000 年铺光纤一样，建多了？
— AI 智能体普及之后，算力需求会变成什么样？
— 送上太空的 TPU，发回了什么？

内容非常精彩，详情请见视频。视频里，我还聊了为什么我认为，之前的科技革命里，后发先至是聪明的，但 AI 时代，只有勇敢的先发者才有可能成功。想要采用后发先至策略的公司，很可能会丢掉一整个时代。

text:
Pool Launch 模式潜力无限，有可能成为未来代币发行与玩法的超级基础设施。但它也赋予了开发者更多权限，和完全统一标准的内盘模式有本质区别。刚上线时，千万不要为了速度盲目FOMO买入，购买前务必重点检查以下两个指标：

1. 筹码分配
重点看开发者有没有预留筹码、预留了多少。代币具体落在哪种地址：
 ·普通地址（随时可能卖出）
 ·OpenTokenDock（未验证的代币分配合约，风险较高，需重点警惕）
 ·VerifiedTokenDock（已验证的分配合约，会公示用途）

2.流动性
看流动性相对市值是否合理。如果流动性明显偏小，一定要结合项目资料和筹码分配一起判断，确认是机制设计还是存在大额预留的作恶风险。

Pool Launch会带来无限可能，但玩这个模式的核心就是盯紧筹码分配和流动性数据。理性参与，Dyor会更重要。

text:
【深圳求职｜25岁｜仓储管理经验＋技术能力＋AI应用】

本人25岁，目前在深圳，正在寻找一份具有发展空间、能够长期积累专业能力的工作，希望有机会加入重视实际能力、工作成果与个人成长的团队。

一、个人背景与技术能力

学历： 本科（非全日制）

专业背景： 大专计算机相关专业，具备一定的技术基础。

技术能力：

掌握 Python、Linux、MySQL 基础知识，能够进行基本的脚本编写、数据库查询及 Linux 环境操作。
熟悉 API 接口调用与基础开发流程，对 FastAPI、LangChain、RAG、AI Agent 等技术有一定的学习与实践经验。
持续关注人工智能技术的发展，注重将新技术应用于真实业务场景，提高工作效率。

二、工作经历与管理成果

目前在深圳一家食品供应链企业担任仓库主管，参与管理多个仓库，管理面积合计约 1000 平方米。

主要负责仓储日常运营、人员安排、现场管理、客户接待、库存管理、损耗控制及跨部门沟通协调，同时推动仓储作业流程的标准化和效率优化。

任职期间主要成果：

分拣准确率提升至 95%。
漏货率降低至 2%。
库存准确率提升至 95%。
优化仓储部门与订单部门的业务流程，减少人工重复操作，提升部门协作效率。
主动发现业务流程中的低效环节，并结合数字化工具提出和推动改进方案。

过去低谷期从事过洗车、外卖配送、快递、保安、电子厂流水线工人等不同岗位。

这些经历让我接触到不同类型的基层业务场景，对一线作业、执行效率、人员协作和实际运营问题有了更直观的理解，也培养了较强的适应能力与执行意识。

三、个人优势

1. 善于发现问题、分析问题并推动解决

不仅关注任务是否完成，也会思考现有流程是否合理、是否存在重复劳动，以及能否通过流程优化或技术工具提升效率。

2. 具有自主学习与实践能力

能够根据实际需求主动学习新知识，对 AI、自动化工具、企业数字化和业务系统开发保持长期兴趣，并尝试将所学技术应用到业务场景中。

3. 兼具一线业务经验与技术理解能力

既了解仓储、物流、供应链等实际业务流程，也具备一定的编程和数据库知识，希望未来能从单纯的执行型工作逐步向业务优化、数字化运营及技术应用方向发展。

4. 做事务实，具备责任意识

愿意深入一线了解问题，能够承担具体工作任务，重视结果交付与持续改进。

四、个人不足与改进方向

性格相对内向，不属于特别外向、善于社交的类型，但不影响正常的业务沟通、跨部门协作和问题处理。

相比于高频社交，我更习惯通过充分了解问题、清晰表达观点和实际工作成果建立信任。

另外，我也清楚自己目前的技术深度和项目经验仍有提升空间，因此一直保持学习，并希望在真实业务环境中进一步积累经验。

五、关于学历

由于个人早期求学经历中的一些客观原因，未能通过传统高考路径进入全日制本科院校。

但我没有因此停止学习，持续自主学习计算机技术与人工智能相关知识。

我理解学历是企业评估候选人的重要参考，但也希望能够通过实际工作成果、学习能力和解决问题的能力，获得更多被了解和考察的机会。

求职期望： 希望加入一家有长期发展空间、愿意培养人才、重视实际能力与贡献的企业。

如果有合适的工作机会，欢迎私信联系。期待进一步沟通，也愿意接受企业对实际能力的考察。
